textMismatch.clean: To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding;
textMismatch.wharton: But his delight [is] in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.

textMismatch.clean: To receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, and judgment, and equity;
textMismatch.wharton: And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

textMismatch.clean: To give subtilty to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion.
textMismatch.wharton: The ungodly [are] not so: but [are] like the chaff which the wind driveth away.

textMismatch.clean: A wise [man] will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:
textMismatch.wharton: Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.

textMismatch.clean: To understand a proverb, and the interpretation; the words of the wise, and their dark sayings.
textMismatch.wharton: For the LORD knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.

textMismatch.clean: MY son, if thou wilt receive my words, and hide my commandments with thee;
textMismatch.wharton: Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?

textMismatch.clean: So that thou incline thine ear unto wisdom, [and] apply thine heart to understanding;
textMismatch.wharton: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his anointed, [saying],

textMismatch.clean: Yea, if thou criest after knowledge, [and] liftest up thy voice for understanding;
textMismatch.wharton: Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.

textMismatch.clean: If thou seekest her as silver, and searchest for her as [for] hid treasures;
textMismatch.wharton: He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision.

textMismatch.clean: Then shalt thou understand the fear of the LORD, and find the knowledge of God.
textMismatch.wharton: Then shall he speak unto them in his wrath, and vex them in his sore displeasure.

textMismatch.clean: For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth [cometh] knowledge and understanding.
textMismatch.wharton: Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion.

textMismatch.clean: He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous: [he] [is] a buckler to them that walk uprightly.
textMismatch.wharton: I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee.

textMismatch.clean: He keepeth the paths of judgment, and preserveth the way of his saints.
textMismatch.wharton: Ask of me, and I shall give [thee] the heathen [for] thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth [for] thy possession.

textMismatch.clean: Then shalt thou understand righteousness, and judgment, and equity; [yea], every good path.
textMismatch.wharton: Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potters vessel.

textMismatch.clean: When wisdom entereth into thine heart, and knowledge is pleasant unto thy soul;
textMismatch.wharton: Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.

textMismatch.clean: Discretion shall preserve thee, understanding shall keep thee:
textMismatch.wharton: Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.

textMismatch.clean: To deliver thee from the way of the evil [man], from the man that speaketh froward things;
textMismatch.wharton: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish [from] the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed [are] all they that put their trust in him.

textMismatch.clean: MY son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments:
textMismatch.wharton: LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many [are] they that rise up against me.

textMismatch.clean: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.
textMismatch.wharton: Many [there be] which say of my soul, [There is] no help for him in God. Selah.

textMismatch.clean: Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:
textMismatch.wharton: But thou, O LORD, [art] a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.

textMismatch.clean: So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
textMismatch.wharton: I cried unto the LORD with my voice, and he heard me out of his holy hill. Selah.

textMismatch.clean: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
textMismatch.wharton: I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.

textMismatch.clean: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
textMismatch.wharton: I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set [themselves] against me round about.

textMismatch.clean: Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the LORD, and depart from evil.
textMismatch.wharton: Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God: for thou hast smitten all mine enemies [upon] the cheek bone; thou hast broken the teeth of the ungodly.

textMismatch.clean: It shall be health to thy navel, and marrow to thy bones.
textMismatch.wharton: Salvation [belongeth] unto the LORD: thy blessing [is] upon thy people. Selah.

textMismatch.clean: HEAR, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding.
textMismatch.wharton: Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me [when I was] in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.

textMismatch.clean: For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.
textMismatch.wharton: O ye sons of men, how long [will ye turn] my glory into shame? [how long] will ye love vanity, [and] seek after leasing? Selah.

textMismatch.clean: For I was my fathers son, tender and only [beloved] in the sight of my mother.
textMismatch.wharton: But know that the LORD hath set apart him that is godly for himself: the LORD will hear when I call unto him.

textMismatch.clean: He taught me also, and said unto me, Let thine heart retain my words: keep my commandments, and live.
textMismatch.wharton: Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.

textMismatch.clean: Get wisdom, get understanding: forget [it] not; neither decline from the words of my mouth.
textMismatch.wharton: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the LORD.

textMismatch.clean: Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee.
textMismatch.wharton: [There be] many that say, Who will shew us [any] good? LORD, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us.

textMismatch.clean: Wisdom [is] the principal thing; [therefore] get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.
textMismatch.wharton: Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time [that] their corn and their wine increased.

textMismatch.clean: Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her.
textMismatch.wharton: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.

textMismatch.clean: MY son, attend unto my wisdom, [and] bow thine ear to my understanding:
textMismatch.wharton: Give ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.

textMismatch.clean: That thou mayest regard discretion, and [that] thy lips may keep knowledge.
textMismatch.wharton: Hearken unto the voice of my cry, my King, and my God: for unto thee will I pray.

textMismatch.clean: For the lips of a strange woman drop [as] an honeycomb, and her mouth [is] smoother than oil:
textMismatch.wharton: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct [my prayer] unto thee, and will look up.

textMismatch.clean: But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a twoedged sword.
textMismatch.wharton: For thou [art] not a God that hath pleasure in wickedness: neither shall evil dwell with thee.

textMismatch.clean: Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell.
textMismatch.wharton: The foolish shall not stand in thy sight: thou hatest all workers of iniquity.

textMismatch.clean: Lest thou shouldest ponder the path of life, her ways are moveable, [that] thou canst not know [them].
textMismatch.wharton: Thou shalt destroy them that speak leasing: the LORD will abhor the bloody and deceitful man.

textMismatch.clean: Hear me now therefore, O ye children, and depart not from the words of my mouth.
textMismatch.wharton: But as for me, I will come [into] thy house in the multitude of thy mercy: [and] in thy fear will I worship toward thy holy temple.

textMismatch.clean: Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the door of her house:
textMismatch.wharton: Lead me, O LORD, in thy righteousness because of mine enemies; make thy way straight before my face.

textMismatch.clean: Lest thou give thine honour unto others, and thy years unto the cruel:
textMismatch.wharton: For [there is] no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part [is] very wickedness; their throat [is] an open sepulchre; they flatter with their tongue.

textMismatch.clean: Lest strangers be filled with thy wealth; and thy labours [be] in the house of a stranger;
textMismatch.wharton: Destroy thou them, O God; let them fall by their own counsels; cast them out in the multitude of their transgressions; for they have rebelled against thee.

textMismatch.clean: And thou mourn at the last, when thy flesh and thy body are consumed,
textMismatch.wharton: But let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice: let them ever shout for joy, because thou defendest them: let them also that love thy name be joyful in thee.

textMismatch.clean: And say, How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof;
textMismatch.wharton: For thou, LORD, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as [with] a shield.

textMismatch.clean: MY son, if thou be surety for thy friend, [if] thou hast stricken thy hand with a stranger,
textMismatch.wharton: O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.

textMismatch.clean: Thou art snared with the words of thy mouth, thou art taken with the words of thy mouth.
textMismatch.wharton: Have mercy upon me, O LORD; for I [am] weak: O LORD, heal me; for my bones are vexed.

textMismatch.clean: Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself, when thou art come into the hand of thy friend; go, humble thyself, and make sure thy friend.
textMismatch.wharton: My soul is also sore vexed: but thou, O LORD, how long?

textMismatch.clean: Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids.
textMismatch.wharton: Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies sake.

textMismatch.clean: Deliver thyself as a roe from the hand [of] [the] [hunter], and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.
textMismatch.wharton: For in death [there is] no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?

textMismatch.clean: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:
textMismatch.wharton: I am weary with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears.

textMismatch.clean: Which having no guide, overseer, or ruler,
textMismatch.wharton: Mine eye is consumed because of grief; it waxeth old because of all mine enemies.

textMismatch.clean: Provideth her meat in the summer, [and] gathereth her food in the harvest.
textMismatch.wharton: Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity; for the LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping.

textMismatch.clean: How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?
textMismatch.wharton: The LORD hath heard my supplication; the LORD will receive my prayer.

textMismatch.clean: [Yet] a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
textMismatch.wharton: Let all mine enemies be ashamed and sore vexed: let them return [and] be ashamed suddenly.

textMismatch.clean: MY son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee.
textMismatch.wharton: O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me:

textMismatch.clean: Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.
textMismatch.wharton: Lest he tear my soul like a lion, rending [it] in pieces, while [there is] none to deliver.

textMismatch.clean: Bind them upon thy fingers, write them upon the table of thine heart.
textMismatch.wharton: O LORD my God, if I have done this; if there be iniquity in my hands;

textMismatch.clean: Say unto wisdom, Thou [art] my sister; and call understanding [thy] kinswoman:
textMismatch.wharton: If I have rewarded evil unto him that was at peace with me; (yea, I have delivered him that without cause is mine enemy:)

textMismatch.clean: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, from the stranger [which] flattereth with her words.
textMismatch.wharton: Let the enemy persecute my soul, and take [it]; yea, let him tread down my life upon the earth, and lay mine honour in the dust. Selah.

textMismatch.clean: For at the window of my house I looked through my casement,
textMismatch.wharton: Arise, O LORD, in thine anger, lift up thyself because of the rage of mine enemies: and awake for me [to] the judgment [that] thou hast commanded.

textMismatch.clean: And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding,
textMismatch.wharton: So shall the congregation of the people compass thee about: for their sakes therefore return thou on high.

textMismatch.clean: Passing through the street near her corner; and he went the way to her house,
textMismatch.wharton: The LORD shall judge the people: judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity [that is] in me.

textMismatch.clean: In the twilight, in the evening, in the black and dark night:
textMismatch.wharton: Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end; but establish the just: for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins.

textMismatch.clean: And, behold, there met him a woman [with] the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.

textMismatch.wharton: If he turn not, he will whet his sword; he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.

textMismatch.clean: So she caught him, and kissed him, [and] with an impudent face said unto him,
textMismatch.wharton: He hath also prepared for him the instruments of death; he ordaineth his arrows against the persecutors.

textMismatch.clean: [I] [have] peace offerings with me; this day have I payed my vows.
textMismatch.wharton: Behold, he travaileth with iniquity, and hath conceived mischief, and brought forth falsehood.

textMismatch.clean: Therefore came I forth to meet thee, diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee.
textMismatch.wharton: He made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch [which] he made.

textMismatch.clean: I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved [works], with fine linen of Egypt.
textMismatch.wharton: His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his violent dealing shall come down upon his own pate.

textMismatch.clean: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
textMismatch.wharton: I will praise the LORD according to his righteousness: and will sing praise to the name of the LORD most high.

textMismatch.clean: DOTH not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?
textMismatch.wharton: O LORD our Lord, how excellent [is] thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.

textMismatch.clean: She standeth in the top of high places, by the way in the places of the paths.
textMismatch.wharton: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger.

textMismatch.clean: She crieth at the gates, at the entry of the city, at the coming in at the doors.
textMismatch.wharton: When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained;

textMismatch.clean: Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice [is] to the sons of man.
textMismatch.wharton: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him?

textMismatch.clean: O ye simple, understand wisdom: and, ye fools, be ye of an understanding heart.
textMismatch.wharton: For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.

textMismatch.clean: Hear; for I will speak of excellent things; and the opening of my lips [shall] [be] right things.
textMismatch.wharton: Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all [things] under his feet:

textMismatch.clean: For my mouth shall speak truth; and wickedness [is] an abomination to my lips.
textMismatch.wharton: All sheep and oxen, yea, and the beasts of the field;

textMismatch.clean: All the words of my mouth [are] in righteousness; [there] [is] nothing froward or perverse in them.
textMismatch.wharton: The fowl of the air, and the fish of the sea, [and whatsoever] passeth through the paths of the seas.

textMismatch.clean: They [are] all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.
textMismatch.wharton: O LORD our Lord, how excellent [is] thy name in all the earth!

textMismatch.clean: WISDOM hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars:
textMismatch.wharton: I will praise [thee], O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.

textMismatch.clean: She hath killed her beasts; she hath mingled her wine; she hath also furnished her table.
textMismatch.wharton: I will be glad and rejoice in thee: I will sing praise to thy name, O thou most High.

textMismatch.clean: She hath sent forth her maidens: she crieth upon the highest places of the city,
textMismatch.wharton: When mine enemies are turned back, they shall fall and perish at thy presence.

textMismatch.clean: Whoso [is] simple, let him turn in hither: [as] [for] him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,
textMismatch.wharton: For thou hast maintained my right and my cause; thou satest in the throne judging right.

textMismatch.clean: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine [which] I have mingled.
textMismatch.wharton: Thou hast rebuked the heathen, thou hast destroyed the wicked, thou hast put out their name for ever and ever.

textMismatch.clean: Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding.
textMismatch.wharton: O thou enemy, destructions are come to a perpetual end: and thou hast destroyed cities; their memorial is perished with them.

textMismatch.clean: He that reproveth a scorner getteth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh a wicked [man] [getteth] himself a blot.
textMismatch.wharton: But the LORD shall endure for ever: he hath prepared his throne for judgment.

textMismatch.clean: Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee: rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.
textMismatch.wharton: And he shall judge the world in righteousness, he shall minister judgment to the people in uprightness.

textMismatch.clean: Give [instruction] to a wise [man], and he will be yet wiser: teach a just [man], and he will increase in learning.
textMismatch.wharton: The LORD also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.

textMismatch.clean: The fear of the LORD [is] the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy [is] understanding.
textMismatch.wharton: And they that know thy name will put their trust in thee: for thou, LORD, hast not forsaken them that seek thee.

textMismatch.clean: For by me thy days shall be multiplied, and the years of thy life shall be increased.
textMismatch.wharton: Sing praises to the LORD, which dwelleth in Zion: declare among the people his doings.

textMismatch.clean: If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself: but [if] thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear [it].
textMismatch.wharton: When he maketh inquisition for blood, he remembereth them: he forgetteth not the cry of the humble.

textMismatch.clean: A foolish woman [is] clamorous: [she] [is] simple, and knoweth nothing.
textMismatch.wharton: Have mercy upon me, O LORD; consider my trouble [which I suffer] of them that hate me, thou that liftest me up from the gates of death:

textMismatch.clean: For she sitteth at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,
textMismatch.wharton: That I may shew forth all thy praise in the gates of the daughter of Zion: I will rejoice in thy salvation.

textMismatch.clean: To call passengers who go right on their ways:
textMismatch.wharton: The heathen are sunk down in the pit [that] they made: in the net which they hid is their own foot taken.

textMismatch.clean: Whoso [is] simple, let him turn in hither: and [as] [for] him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,
textMismatch.wharton: The LORD is known [by] the judgment [which] he executeth: the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah.

textMismatch.clean: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread [eaten] in secret is pleasant.
textMismatch.wharton: The wicked shall be turned into hell, [and] all the nations that forget God.

textMismatch.clean: But he knoweth not that the dead [are] there; [and] [that] her guests [are] in the depths of hell.
textMismatch.wharton: For the needy shall not alway be forgotten: the expectation of the poor shall [not] perish for ever.

textMismatch.clean: THE proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish son [is] the heaviness of his mother.
textMismatch.wharton: Why standest thou afar off, O LORD? [why] hidest thou [thyself] in times of trouble?

textMismatch.clean: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivereth from death.
textMismatch.wharton: The wicked in [his] pride doth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the devices that they have imagined.

textMismatch.clean: The LORD will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish: but he casteth away the substance of the wicked.
textMismatch.wharton: For the wicked boasteth of his hearts desire, and blesseth the covetous, [whom] the LORD abhorreth.

textMismatch.clean: He becometh poor that dealeth [with] a slack hand: but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.
textMismatch.wharton: The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek [after God]: God [is] not in all his thoughts.

textMismatch.clean: He that gathereth in summer [is] a wise son: [but] he that sleepeth in harvest [is] a son that causeth shame.
textMismatch.wharton: His ways are always grievous; thy judgments [are] far above out of his sight: [as for] all his enemies, he puffeth at them.

textMismatch.clean: Blessings [are] upon the head of the just: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
textMismatch.wharton: He hath said in his heart, I shall not be moved: for [I shall] never [be] in adversity.

textMismatch.clean: The memory of the just [is] blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot.
textMismatch.wharton: His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and fraud: under his tongue [is] mischief and vanity.

textMismatch.clean: The wise in heart will receive commandments: but a prating fool shall fall.
textMismatch.wharton: He sitteth in the lurking places of the villages: in the secret places doth he murder the innocent: his eyes are privily set against the poor.

textMismatch.clean: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.
textMismatch.wharton: He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den: he lieth in wait to catch the poor: he doth catch the poor, when he draweth him into his net.

textMismatch.clean: He that winketh with the eye causeth sorrow: but a prating fool shall fall.
textMismatch.wharton: He croucheth, [and] humbleth himself, that the poor may fall by his strong ones.

textMismatch.clean: The mouth of a righteous [man] [is] a well of life: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
textMismatch.wharton: He hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten: he hideth his face; he will never see [it].

textMismatch.clean: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.
textMismatch.wharton: Arise, O LORD; O God, lift up thine hand: forget not the humble.

textMismatch.clean: In the lips of him that hath understanding wisdom is found: but a rod [is] for the back of him that is void of understanding.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore doth the wicked contemn God? he hath said in his heart, Thou wilt not require [it].

textMismatch.clean: Wise [men] lay up knowledge: but the mouth of the foolish [is] near destruction.
textMismatch.wharton: Thou hast seen [it]; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite [it] with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless.

textMismatch.clean: The rich mans wealth [is] his strong city: the destruction of the poor [is] their poverty.
textMismatch.wharton: Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil [man]: seek out his wickedness [till] thou find none.

textMismatch.clean: The labour of the righteous [tendeth] to life: the fruit of the wicked to sin.
textMismatch.wharton: The LORD [is] King for ever and ever: the heathen are perished out of his land.

textMismatch.clean: He [is] [in] the way of life that keepeth instruction: but he that refuseth reproof erreth.
textMismatch.wharton: LORD, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear:

textMismatch.clean: He that hideth hatred [with] lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, [is] a fool.
textMismatch.wharton: To judge the fatherless and the oppressed, that the man of the earth may no more oppress.

textMismatch.clean: WHOSO loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof [is] brutish.
textMismatch.wharton: Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men.

textMismatch.clean: A good [man] obtaineth favour of the LORD: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn.
textMismatch.wharton: They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: [with] flattering lips [and] with a double heart do they speak.

textMismatch.clean: A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.

textMismatch.clean: A virtuous woman [is] a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed [is] as rottenness in his bones.
textMismatch.wharton: Who have said, With our tongue will we prevail; our lips [are] our own: who [is] lord over us?

textMismatch.clean: The thoughts of the righteous [are] right: [but] the counsels of the wicked [are] deceit.
textMismatch.wharton: For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, now will I arise, saith the LORD; I will set [him] in safety [from him that] puffeth at him.

textMismatch.clean: The words of the wicked [are] to lie in wait for blood: but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.

textMismatch.clean: And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give [it] thee, unto the half of my kingdom.
textMismatch.wharton: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great [is] that darkness!

textMismatch.clean: And she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.
textMismatch.wharton: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

textMismatch.clean: And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist.
textMismatch.wharton: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?

textMismatch.clean: And the king was exceeding sorry; [yet] for his oaths sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her.
textMismatch.wharton: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?

textMismatch.clean: And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
textMismatch.wharton: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?

textMismatch.clean: And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.
textMismatch.wharton: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:

textMismatch.clean: And when his disciples heard [of] [it], they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
textMismatch.wharton: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

textMismatch.clean: And the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, [shall he] not much more [clothe] you, O ye of little faith?

textMismatch.clean: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
textMismatch.wharton: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?

textMismatch.clean: And they departed into a desert place by ship privately.
textMismatch.wharton: (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.

textMismatch.clean: And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran afoot thither out of all cities, and outwent them, and came together unto him.
textMismatch.wharton: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

textMismatch.clean: And Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.
textMismatch.wharton: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day [is] the evil thereof.

textMismatch.clean: THEN came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.
textMismatch.wharton: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

textMismatch.clean: And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.
textMismatch.wharton: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.

textMismatch.clean: For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash [their] hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.
textMismatch.wharton: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brothers eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

textMismatch.clean: And [when] [they] [come] from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, [as] the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.
textMismatch.wharton: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam [is] in thine own eye?

textMismatch.clean: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?
textMismatch.wharton: Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brothers eye.

textMismatch.clean: He answered and said unto them, Well hath Esaias prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth me with [their] lips, but their heart is far from me.
textMismatch.wharton: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.

textMismatch.clean: Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching [for] doctrines the commandments of men.
textMismatch.wharton: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

textMismatch.clean: For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, [as] the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.
textMismatch.wharton: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

textMismatch.clean: And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.
textMismatch.wharton: Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone?

textMismatch.clean: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:
textMismatch.wharton: Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent?

textMismatch.clean: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, [It] [is] Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; [he] [shall] [be] [free].
textMismatch.wharton: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

textMismatch.clean: And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;
textMismatch.wharton: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

textMismatch.clean: Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.
textMismatch.wharton: Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide [is] the gate, and broad [is] the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:

textMismatch.clean: And when he had called all the people [unto] [him], he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one [of] [you], and understand:
textMismatch.wharton: Because strait [is] the gate, and narrow [is] the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.

textMismatch.clean: There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.
textMismatch.wharton: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheeps clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

textMismatch.clean: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.
textMismatch.wharton: Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

textMismatch.clean: And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.
textMismatch.wharton: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

textMismatch.clean: And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, [it] cannot defile him;
textMismatch.wharton: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither [can] a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

textMismatch.clean: Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?
textMismatch.wharton: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

textMismatch.clean: And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.

textMismatch.clean: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
textMismatch.wharton: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.

textMismatch.clean: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:
textMismatch.wharton: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?

textMismatch.clean: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.
textMismatch.wharton: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

textMismatch.clean: And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know [it:] but he could not be hid.
textMismatch.wharton: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:

textMismatch.clean: For a [certain] woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:
textMismatch.wharton: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

textMismatch.clean: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.
textMismatch.wharton: And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand:

textMismatch.clean: But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the childrens bread, and to cast [it] unto the dogs.
textMismatch.wharton: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it.

textMismatch.clean: And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the childrens crumbs.
textMismatch.wharton: And it came to pass, when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at his doctrine:

textMismatch.clean: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.
textMismatch.wharton: For he taught them as [one] having authority, and not as the scribes.

textMismatch.clean: IN those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples [unto] [him], and saith unto them,
textMismatch.wharton: When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

textMismatch.clean: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat:
textMismatch.wharton: And, behold, there came a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

textMismatch.clean: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far.
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus put forth [his] hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou clean. And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

textMismatch.clean: And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these [men] with bread here in the wilderness?
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man; but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

textMismatch.clean: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.
textMismatch.wharton: And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,

textMismatch.clean: And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and brake, and gave to his disciples to set before [them;] and they did set [them] before the people.
textMismatch.wharton: And saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.

textMismatch.clean: And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before [them].
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him.

textMismatch.clean: So they did eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken [meat] that was left seven baskets.
textMismatch.wharton: The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.

textMismatch.clean: And they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he sent them away.
textMismatch.wharton: For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this [man], Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth [it].

textMismatch.clean: And straightway he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
textMismatch.wharton: When Jesus heard [it], he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

textMismatch.clean: And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, tempting him.
textMismatch.wharton: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.

textMismatch.clean: And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.
textMismatch.wharton: But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

textMismatch.clean: And he left them, and entering into the ship again departed to the other side.
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, [so] be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.

textMismatch.clean: Now [the] [disciples] had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more than one loaf.
textMismatch.wharton: And when Jesus was come into Peters house, he saw his wifes mother laid, and sick of a fever.

textMismatch.clean: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and [of] the leaven of Herod.
textMismatch.wharton: And he touched her hand, and the fever left her: and she arose, and ministered unto them.

textMismatch.clean: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, [It] [is] because we have no bread.
textMismatch.wharton: When the even was come, they brought unto him many that were possessed with devils: and he cast out the spirits with [his] word, and healed all that were sick:

textMismatch.clean: And when Jesus knew [it], he saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened?
textMismatch.wharton: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare [our] sicknesses.

textMismatch.clean: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?
textMismatch.wharton: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandment to depart unto the other side.

textMismatch.clean: When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? They say unto him, Twelve.
textMismatch.wharton: And a certain scribe came, and said unto him, Master, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.

textMismatch.clean: And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? And they said, Seven.
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air [have] nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay [his] head.

textMismatch.clean: And he said unto them, How is it that ye do not understand?
textMismatch.wharton: And another of his disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.

textMismatch.clean: And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.
textMismatch.wharton: But Jesus said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.

textMismatch.clean: And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought.
textMismatch.wharton: And when he was entered into a ship, his disciples followed him.

textMismatch.clean: And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.
textMismatch.wharton: And, behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the ship was covered with the waves: but he was asleep.

textMismatch.clean: After that he put [his] hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.
textMismatch.wharton: And his disciples came to [him], and awoke him, saying, Lord, save us: we perish.

textMismatch.clean: And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell [it] to any in the town.
textMismatch.wharton: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.

textMismatch.clean: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Cæsarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?
textMismatch.wharton: But the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!

textMismatch.clean: And they answered, John the Baptist: but some [say], Elias; and others, One of the prophets.
textMismatch.wharton: And when he was come to the other side into the country of the Gergesenes, there met him two possessed with devils, coming out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man might pass by that way.

textMismatch.clean: And he saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?

textMismatch.clean: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.
textMismatch.wharton: And there was a good way off from them an herd of many swine feeding.

textMismatch.clean: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and [of] the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
textMismatch.wharton: So the devils besought him, saying, If thou cast us out, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine.

textMismatch.clean: And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.
textMismatch.wharton: And he said unto them, Go. And when they were come out, they went into the herd of swine: and, behold, the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters.

textMismatch.clean: But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.
textMismatch.wharton: And they that kept them fled, and went their ways into the city, and told every thing, and what was befallen to the possessed of the devils.

textMismatch.clean: And when he had called the people [unto] [him] with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
textMismatch.wharton: And, behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus: and when they saw him, they besought [him] that he would depart out of their coasts.

textMismatch.clean: AND he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.
textMismatch.wharton: And he entered into a ship, and passed over, and came into his own city.

textMismatch.clean: And after six days Jesus taketh [with] [him] Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them.
textMismatch.wharton: And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.

textMismatch.clean: And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.
textMismatch.wharton: And, behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, This [man] blasphemeth.

textMismatch.clean: And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?

textMismatch.clean: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
textMismatch.wharton: For whether is easier, to say, [Thy] sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk?

textMismatch.clean: For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.
textMismatch.wharton: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (then saith he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house.

textMismatch.clean: And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
textMismatch.wharton: And he arose, and departed to his house.

textMismatch.clean: And suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.
textMismatch.wharton: But when the multitudes saw [it], they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men.

textMismatch.clean: And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of man were risen from the dead.
textMismatch.wharton: And as Jesus passed forth from thence, he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.

textMismatch.clean: And they kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean.
textMismatch.wharton: And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.

textMismatch.clean: And they asked him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elias must first come?
textMismatch.wharton: And when the Pharisees saw [it], they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?

textMismatch.clean: And he answered and told them, Elias verily cometh first, and restoreth all things; and how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at nought.
textMismatch.wharton: But when Jesus heard [that], he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.

textMismatch.clean: But I say unto you, That Elias is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed, as it is written of him.
textMismatch.wharton: But go ye and learn what [that] meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

textMismatch.clean: And when he came to [his] disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them.
textMismatch.wharton: Then came to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast oft, but thy disciples fast not?

textMismatch.clean: And straightway all the people, when they beheld him, were greatly amazed, and running to [him] saluted him.
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.

textMismatch.clean: And he asked the scribes, What question ye with them?
textMismatch.wharton: No man putteth a piece of new cloth unto an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up taketh from the garment, and the rent is made worse.

textMismatch.clean: And one of the multitude answered and said, Master, I have brought unto thee my son, which hath a dumb spirit;
textMismatch.wharton: Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.

textMismatch.clean: And wheresoever he taketh him, he teareth him: and he foameth, and gnasheth with his teeth, and pineth away: and I spake to thy disciples that they should cast him out; and they could not.
textMismatch.wharton: While he spake these things unto them, behold, there came a certain ruler, and worshipped him, saying, My daughter is even now dead: but come and lay thy hand upon her, and she shall live.

textMismatch.clean: He answereth him, and saith, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him unto me.
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus arose, and followed him, and [so did] his disciples.

textMismatch.clean: And they brought him unto him: and when he saw him, straightway the spirit tare him; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed foaming.
textMismatch.wharton: And, behold, a woman, which was diseased with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind [him], and touched the hem of his garment:

textMismatch.clean: And he asked his father, How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child.
textMismatch.wharton: For she said within herself, If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole.

textMismatch.clean: And ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him: but if thou canst do any thing, have compassion on us, and help us.
textMismatch.wharton: But Jesus turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.

textMismatch.clean: Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things [are] possible to him that believeth.
textMismatch.wharton: And when Jesus came into the rulers house, and saw the minstrels and the people making a noise,

textMismatch.clean: And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
textMismatch.wharton: He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn.

textMismatch.clean: When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the foul spirit, saying unto him, [Thou] dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.
textMismatch.wharton: But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose.

textMismatch.clean: And [the] [spirit] cried, and rent him sore, and came out of him: and he was as one dead; insomuch that many said, He is dead.
textMismatch.wharton: And the fame hereof went abroad into all that land.

textMismatch.clean: But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up; and he arose.
textMismatch.wharton: And when Jesus departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, [Thou] Son of David, have mercy on us.
