textMismatch.clean: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak unto the people concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness for to see? A reed shaken with the wind?
textMismatch.wharton: And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know [it]: but he could not be hid.

textMismatch.clean: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they which are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings courts.
textMismatch.wharton: For a [certain] woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:

textMismatch.clean: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.
textMismatch.wharton: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.

textMismatch.clean: This is [he], of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
textMismatch.wharton: But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the childrens bread, and to cast [it] unto the dogs.

textMismatch.clean: For I say unto you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
textMismatch.wharton: And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the childrens crumbs.

textMismatch.clean: And all the people that heard [him], and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.
textMismatch.wharton: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.

textMismatch.clean: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.
textMismatch.wharton: And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.

textMismatch.clean: And the Lord said, Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?
textMismatch.wharton: And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.

textMismatch.clean: They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.
textMismatch.wharton: And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to put his hand upon him.

textMismatch.clean: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a devil.
textMismatch.wharton: And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue;

textMismatch.clean: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners!
textMismatch.wharton: And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.

textMismatch.clean: But wisdom is justified of all her children.
textMismatch.wharton: And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.

textMismatch.clean: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisees house, and sat down to meat.
textMismatch.wharton: And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published [it];

textMismatch.clean: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that [Jesus] sat at meat in the Pharisees house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,
textMismatch.wharton: And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.

textMismatch.clean: AND it came to pass afterward, that he went throughout every city and village, preaching and shewing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God: and the twelve [were] with him,
textMismatch.wharton: In those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples [unto him], and saith unto them,

textMismatch.clean: And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils,
textMismatch.wharton: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat:

textMismatch.clean: And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herods steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance.
textMismatch.wharton: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far.

textMismatch.clean: And when much people were gathered together, and were come to him out of every city, he spake by a parable:
textMismatch.wharton: And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these [men] with bread here in the wilderness?

textMismatch.clean: A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.
textMismatch.wharton: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.

textMismatch.clean: And some fell upon a rock; and as soon as it was sprung up, it withered away, because it lacked moisture.
textMismatch.wharton: And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and brake, and gave to his disciples to set before [them]; and they did set [them] before the people.

textMismatch.clean: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.
textMismatch.wharton: And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before [them].

textMismatch.clean: And other fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bare fruit an hundredfold. And when he had said these things, he cried, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
textMismatch.wharton: So they did eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken [meat] that was left seven baskets.

textMismatch.clean: And his disciples asked him, saying, What might this parable be?
textMismatch.wharton: And they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he sent them away.

textMismatch.clean: And he said, Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God: but to others in parables; that seeing they might not see, and hearing they might not understand.
textMismatch.wharton: And straightway he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.

textMismatch.clean: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
textMismatch.wharton: And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, tempting him.

textMismatch.clean: Those by the way side are they that hear; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.
textMismatch.wharton: And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.

textMismatch.clean: They on the rock [are] [they], which, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.
textMismatch.wharton: And he left them, and entering into the ship again departed to the other side.

textMismatch.clean: And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of [this] life, and bring no fruit to perfection.
textMismatch.wharton: Now [the disciples] had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more than one loaf.

textMismatch.clean: But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep [it], and bring forth fruit with patience.
textMismatch.wharton: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and [of] the leaven of Herod.

textMismatch.clean: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, covereth it with a vessel, or putteth [it] under a bed; but setteth [it] on a candlestick, that they which enter in may see the light.
textMismatch.wharton: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, [It is] because we have no bread.

textMismatch.clean: For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither [any] [thing] hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.
textMismatch.wharton: And when Jesus knew [it], he saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened?

textMismatch.clean: Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given; and whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he seemeth to have.
textMismatch.wharton: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?

textMismatch.clean: Then came to him [his] mother and his brethren, and could not come at him for the press.
textMismatch.wharton: When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? They say unto him, Twelve.

textMismatch.clean: And it was told him [by] [certain] which said, Thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to see thee.
textMismatch.wharton: And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? And they said, Seven.

textMismatch.clean: And he answered and said unto them, My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it.
textMismatch.wharton: And he said unto them, How is it that ye do not understand?

textMismatch.clean: Now it came to pass on a certain day, that he went into a ship with his disciples: and he said unto them, Let us go over unto the other side of the lake. And they launched forth.
textMismatch.wharton: And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.

textMismatch.clean: But as they sailed he fell asleep: and there came down a storm of wind on the lake; and they were filled [with] [water], and were in jeopardy.
textMismatch.wharton: And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought.

textMismatch.clean: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. Then he arose, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calm.
textMismatch.wharton: And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.

textMismatch.clean: And he said unto them, Where is your faith? And they being afraid wondered, saying one to another, What manner of man is this! for he commandeth even the winds and water, and they obey him.
textMismatch.wharton: After that he put [his] hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.

textMismatch.clean: And they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is over against Galilee.
textMismatch.wharton: And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell [it] to any in the town.

textMismatch.clean: And when he went forth to land, there met him out of the city a certain man, which had devils long time, and ware no clothes, neither abode in [any] house, but in the tombs.
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?

textMismatch.clean: When he saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, [thou] Son of God most high? I beseech thee, torment me not.
textMismatch.wharton: And they answered, John the Baptist: but some [say], Elias; and others, One of the prophets.

textMismatch.clean: (For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For oftentimes it had caught him: and he was kept bound with chains and in fetters; and he brake the bands, and was driven of the devil into the wilderness.)
textMismatch.wharton: And he saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.

textMismatch.clean: And Jesus asked him, saying, What is thy name? And he said, Legion: because many devils were entered into him.
textMismatch.wharton: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.

textMismatch.clean: And they besought him that he would not command them to go out into the deep.
textMismatch.wharton: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and [of] the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.

textMismatch.clean: And there was there an herd of many swine feeding on the mountain: and they besought him that he would suffer them to enter into them. And he suffered them.
textMismatch.wharton: And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.

textMismatch.clean: Then went the devils out of the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the lake, and were choked.
textMismatch.wharton: But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.

textMismatch.clean: When they that fed [them] saw what was done, they fled, and went and told [it] in the city and in the country.
textMismatch.wharton: And when he had called the people [unto him] with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

textMismatch.clean: Then they went out to see what was done; and came to Jesus, and found the man, out of whom the devils were departed, sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.
textMismatch.wharton: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospels, the same shall save it.

textMismatch.clean: They also which saw [it] told them by what means he that was possessed of the devils was healed.
textMismatch.wharton: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?

textMismatch.clean: Then the whole multitude of the country of the Gadarenes round about besought him to depart from them; for they were taken with great fear: and he went up into the ship, and returned back again.
textMismatch.wharton: Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

textMismatch.clean: Now the man out of whom the devils were departed besought him that he might be with him: but Jesus sent him away, saying,
textMismatch.wharton: Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

textMismatch.clean: THEN he called his twelve disciples together, and gave them power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases.
textMismatch.wharton: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.

textMismatch.clean: And he sent them to preach the kingdom of God, and to heal the sick.
textMismatch.wharton: And after six days Jesus taketh [with him] Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them.

textMismatch.clean: And he said unto them, Take nothing for [your] journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece.
textMismatch.wharton: And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.

textMismatch.clean: And whatsoever house ye enter into, there abide, and thence depart.
textMismatch.wharton: And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.

textMismatch.clean: And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
textMismatch.wharton: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

textMismatch.clean: And they departed, and went through the towns, preaching the gospel, and healing every where.
textMismatch.wharton: For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.

textMismatch.clean: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him: and he was perplexed, because that it was said of some, that John was risen from the dead;
textMismatch.wharton: And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.

textMismatch.clean: And of some, that Elias had appeared; and of others, that one of the old prophets was risen again.
textMismatch.wharton: And suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.

textMismatch.clean: And Herod said, John have I beheaded: but who is this, of whom I hear such things? And he desired to see him.
textMismatch.wharton: And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of man were risen from the dead.

textMismatch.clean: And the apostles, when they were returned, told him all that they had done. And he took them, and went aside privately into a desert place belonging to the city called Bethsaida.
textMismatch.wharton: And they kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean.

textMismatch.clean: And the people, when they knew [it], followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.
textMismatch.wharton: And they asked him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elias must first come?

textMismatch.clean: And when the day began to wear away, then came the twelve, and said unto him, Send the multitude away, that they may go into the towns and country round about, and lodge, and get victuals: for we are here in a desert place.
textMismatch.wharton: And he answered and told them, Elias verily cometh first, and restoreth all things; and how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at nought.

textMismatch.clean: But he said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they said, We have no more but five loaves and two fishes; except we should go and buy meat for all this people.
textMismatch.wharton: But I say unto you, That Elias is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed, as it is written of him.

textMismatch.clean: For they were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples, Make them sit down by fifties in a company.
textMismatch.wharton: And when he came to [his] disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them.

textMismatch.clean: And they did so, and made them all sit down.
textMismatch.wharton: And straightway all the people, when they beheld him, were greatly amazed, and running to [him] saluted him.

textMismatch.clean: Then he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed them, and brake, and gave to the disciples to set before the multitude.
textMismatch.wharton: And he asked the scribes, What question ye with them?

textMismatch.clean: And they did eat, and were all filled: and there was taken up of fragments that remained to them twelve baskets.
textMismatch.wharton: And one of the multitude answered and said, Master, I have brought unto thee my son, which hath a dumb spirit;

textMismatch.clean: And it came to pass, as he was alone praying, his disciples were with him: and he asked them, saying, Whom say the people that I am?
textMismatch.wharton: And wheresoever he taketh him, he teareth him: and he foameth, and gnasheth with his teeth, and pineth away: and I spake to thy disciples that they should cast him out; and they could not.

textMismatch.clean: They answering said, John the Baptist; but some [say], Elias; and others [say], that one of the old prophets is risen again.
textMismatch.wharton: He answereth him, and saith, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him unto me.

textMismatch.clean: He said unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God.
textMismatch.wharton: And they brought him unto him: and when he saw him, straightway the spirit tare him; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed foaming.

textMismatch.clean: And he straitly charged them, and commanded [them] to tell no man that thing;
textMismatch.wharton: And he asked his father, How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child.

textMismatch.clean: Saying, The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and be raised the third day.
textMismatch.wharton: And ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him: but if thou canst do any thing, have compassion on us, and help us.

textMismatch.clean: And he said to [them] all, If any [man] will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.
textMismatch.wharton: Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things [are] possible to him that believeth.

textMismatch.clean: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it.
textMismatch.wharton: And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

textMismatch.clean: For what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?
textMismatch.wharton: When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the foul spirit, saying unto him, [Thou] dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.

textMismatch.clean: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he shall come in his own glory, and [in] [his] Fathers, and of the holy angels.
textMismatch.wharton: And [the spirit] cried, and rent him sore, and came out of him: and he was as one dead; insomuch that many said, He is dead.

textMismatch.clean: But I tell you of a truth, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God.
textMismatch.wharton: But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up; and he arose.

textMismatch.clean: And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.
textMismatch.wharton: And when he was come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, Why could not we cast him out?

textMismatch.clean: And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment [was] white [and] glistering.
textMismatch.wharton: And he said unto them, This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.

textMismatch.clean: And, behold, there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias:
textMismatch.wharton: And they departed thence, and passed through Galilee; and he would not that any man should know [it].

textMismatch.clean: Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.
textMismatch.wharton: For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Son of man is delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and after that he is killed, he shall rise the third day.

textMismatch.clean: But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.
textMismatch.wharton: But they understood not that saying, and were afraid to ask him.

textMismatch.clean: And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias: not knowing what he said.
textMismatch.wharton: And he came to Capernaum: and being in the house he asked them, What was it that ye disputed among yourselves by the way?

textMismatch.clean: While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.
textMismatch.wharton: But they held their peace: for by the way they had disputed among themselves, who [should be] the greatest.

textMismatch.clean: And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
textMismatch.wharton: And he sat down, and called the twelve, and saith unto them, If any man desire to be first, [the same] shall be last of all, and servant of all.

textMismatch.clean: And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept [it] close, and told no man in those days any of those things which they had seen.
textMismatch.wharton: And he took a child, and set him in the midst of them: and when he had taken him in his arms, he said unto them,

textMismatch.clean: And it came to pass, that on the next day, when they were come down from the hill, much people met him.
textMismatch.wharton: Whosoever shall receive one of such children in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.

textMismatch.clean: And, behold, a man of the company cried out, saying, Master, I beseech thee, look upon my son: for he is mine only child.
textMismatch.wharton: And John answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him, because he followeth not us.

textMismatch.clean: And, lo, a spirit taketh him, and he suddenly crieth out; and it teareth him that he foameth again, and bruising him hardly departeth from him.
textMismatch.wharton: But Jesus said, Forbid him not: for there is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me.

textMismatch.clean: And I besought thy disciples to cast him out; and they could not.
textMismatch.wharton: For he that is not against us is on our part.

textMismatch.clean: And Jesus answering said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you, and suffer you? Bring thy son hither.
textMismatch.wharton: For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because ye belong to Christ, verily I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward.

textMismatch.clean: And as he was yet a coming, the devil threw him down, and tare [him]. And Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the child, and delivered him again to his father.
textMismatch.wharton: And whosoever shall offend one of [these] little ones that believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.

textMismatch.clean: And they were all amazed at the mighty power of God. But while they wondered every one at all things which Jesus did, he said unto his disciples,
textMismatch.wharton: And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:

textMismatch.clean: Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men.
textMismatch.wharton: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

textMismatch.clean: But they understood not this saying, and it was hid from them, that they perceived it not: and they feared to ask him of that saying.
textMismatch.wharton: And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:

textMismatch.clean: Then there arose a reasoning among them, which of them should be greatest.
textMismatch.wharton: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

textMismatch.clean: And Jesus, perceiving the thought of their heart, took a child, and set him by him,
textMismatch.wharton: And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire:

textMismatch.clean: And said unto them, Whosoever shall receive this child in my name receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, the same shall be great.
textMismatch.wharton: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

textMismatch.clean: And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us.

textMismatch.clean: Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.
textMismatch.wharton: And, behold, men brought in a bed a man which was taken with a palsy: and they sought [means] to bring him in, and to lay [him] before him.

textMismatch.clean: Then answered Jesus and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.
textMismatch.wharton: And when they could not find by what [way] they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with [his] couch into the midst before Jesus.

textMismatch.clean: For the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all things that himself doeth: and he will shew him greater works than these, that ye may marvel.
textMismatch.wharton: And when he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.

textMismatch.clean: For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth [them;] even so the Son quickeneth whom he will.
textMismatch.wharton: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?

textMismatch.clean: For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son:
textMismatch.wharton: But when Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answering said unto them, What reason ye in your hearts?

textMismatch.clean: That all [men] should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father which hath sent him.
textMismatch.wharton: Whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Rise up and walk?

textMismatch.clean: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.
textMismatch.wharton: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said unto the sick of the palsy,) I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go into thine house.

textMismatch.clean: Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live.
textMismatch.wharton: And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his own house, glorifying God.

textMismatch.clean: For as the Father hath life in himself; so hath he given to the Son to have life in himself;
textMismatch.wharton: And they were all amazed, and they glorified God, and were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to day.

textMismatch.clean: And hath given him authority to execute judgment also, because he is the Son of man.
textMismatch.wharton: And after these things he went forth, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said unto him, Follow me.

textMismatch.clean: Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice,
textMismatch.wharton: And he left all, rose up, and followed him.

textMismatch.clean: And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.
textMismatch.wharton: And Levi made him a great feast in his own house: and there was a great company of publicans and of others that sat down with them.

textMismatch.clean: I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.
textMismatch.wharton: But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with publicans and sinners?

textMismatch.clean: If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true.
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick.

textMismatch.clean: There is another that beareth witness of me; and I know that the witness which he witnesseth of me is true.
textMismatch.wharton: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

textMismatch.clean: Ye sent unto John, and he bare witness unto the truth.
textMismatch.wharton: And they said unto him, Why do the disciples of John fast often, and make prayers, and likewise [the disciples] of the Pharisees; but thine eat and drink?

textMismatch.clean: But I receive not testimony from man: but these things I say, that ye might be saved.
textMismatch.wharton: And he said unto them, Can ye make the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?

textMismatch.clean: He was a burning and a shining light: and ye were willing for a season to rejoice in his light.
textMismatch.wharton: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.

textMismatch.clean: But I have greater witness than [that] of John: for the works which the Father hath given me to finish, the same works that I do, bear witness of me, that the Father hath sent me.
textMismatch.wharton: And he spake also a parable unto them; No man putteth a piece of a new garment upon an old; if otherwise, then both the new maketh a rent, and the piece that was [taken] out of the new agreeth not with the old.

textMismatch.clean: And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.
textMismatch.wharton: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish.

textMismatch.clean: And ye have not his word abiding in you: for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not.
textMismatch.wharton: But new wine must be put into new bottles; and both are preserved.

textMismatch.clean: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.
textMismatch.wharton: No man also having drunk old [wine] straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.

textMismatch.clean: AFTER these things Jesus went over the sea of Galilee, which is [the] [sea] of Tiberias.
textMismatch.wharton: And it came to pass on the second sabbath after the first, that he went through the corn fields; and his disciples plucked the ears of corn, and did eat, rubbing [them] in [their] hands.

textMismatch.clean: And a great multitude followed him, because they saw his miracles which he did on them that were diseased.
textMismatch.wharton: And certain of the Pharisees said unto them, Why do ye that which is not lawful to do on the sabbath days?

textMismatch.clean: And Jesus went up into a mountain, and there he sat with his disciples.
textMismatch.wharton: And Jesus answering them said, Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungred, and they which were with him;

textMismatch.clean: And the passover, a feast of the Jews, was nigh.
textMismatch.wharton: How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the shewbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?

textMismatch.clean: When Jesus then lifted up [his] eyes, and saw a great company come unto him, he saith unto Philip, Whence shall we buy bread, that these may eat?
textMismatch.wharton: And he said unto them, That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

textMismatch.clean: And this he said to prove him: for he himself knew what he would do.
textMismatch.wharton: And it came to pass also on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered.

textMismatch.clean: Philip answered him, Two hundred pennyworth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may take a little.
textMismatch.wharton: And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath day; that they might find an accusation against him.

textMismatch.clean: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peters brother, saith unto him,
textMismatch.wharton: But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man which had the withered hand, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.

textMismatch.clean: There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?
textMismatch.wharton: Then said Jesus unto them, I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the sabbath days to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy [it]?

textMismatch.clean: And Jesus said, Make the men sit down. Now there was much grass in the place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
textMismatch.wharton: And looking round about upon them all, he said unto the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored whole as the other.

textMismatch.clean: And Jesus took the loaves; and when he had given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to them that were set down; and likewise of the fishes as much as they would.
textMismatch.wharton: And they were filled with madness; and communed one with another what they might do to Jesus.

textMismatch.clean: When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.
textMismatch.wharton: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.

textMismatch.clean: Therefore they gathered [them] together, and filled twelve baskets with the fragments of the five barley loaves, which remained over and above unto them that had eaten.
textMismatch.wharton: And when it was day, he called [unto him] his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;

textMismatch.clean: Then those men, when they had seen the miracle that Jesus did, said, This is of a truth that prophet that should come into the world.
textMismatch.wharton: Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,

textMismatch.clean: When Jesus therefore perceived that they would come and take him by force, to make him a king, he departed again into a mountain himself alone.
textMismatch.wharton: Matthew and Thomas, James the [son] of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zelotes,

textMismatch.clean: And when even was [now] come, his disciples went down unto the sea,
textMismatch.wharton: And Judas [the brother] of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

textMismatch.clean: And entered into a ship, and went over the sea toward Capernaum. And it was now dark, and Jesus was not come to them.
textMismatch.wharton: And he came down with them, and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judaea and Jerusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;

textMismatch.clean: And the sea arose by reason of a great wind that blew.
textMismatch.wharton: And they that were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed.

textMismatch.clean: So when they had rowed about five and twenty or thirty furlongs, they see Jesus walking on the sea, and drawing nigh unto the ship: and they were afraid.
textMismatch.wharton: And the whole multitude sought to touch him: for there went virtue out of him, and healed [them] all.

textMismatch.clean: But he saith unto them, It is I; be not afraid.
textMismatch.wharton: And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed [be ye] poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.

textMismatch.clean: Then they willingly received him into the ship: and immediately the ship was at the land whither they went.
textMismatch.wharton: Blessed [are ye] that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed [are ye] that weep now: for ye shall laugh.

textMismatch.clean: The day following, when the people which stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was none other boat there, save that one whereinto his disciples were entered, and that Jesus went not with his disciples into the boat, but [that] his disciples were gone away alone;
textMismatch.wharton: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you [from their company], and shall reproach [you], and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of mans sake.

textMismatch.clean: (Howbeit there came other boats from Tiberias nigh unto the place where they did eat bread, after that the Lord had given thanks:)
textMismatch.wharton: Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward [is] great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.

textMismatch.clean: When the people therefore saw that Jesus was not there, neither his disciples, they also took shipping, and came to Capernaum, seeking for Jesus.
textMismatch.wharton: But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.

textMismatch.clean: And when they had found him on the other side of the sea, they said unto him, Rabbi, when camest thou hither?
textMismatch.wharton: Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.

textMismatch.clean: Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye saw the miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and were filled.
textMismatch.wharton: Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.

textMismatch.clean: Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed.
textMismatch.wharton: But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you,

textMismatch.clean: Then said they unto him, What shall we do, that we might work the works of God?
textMismatch.wharton: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.

textMismatch.clean: Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.
textMismatch.wharton: And unto him that smiteth thee on the [one] cheek offer also the other; and him that taketh away thy cloke forbid not [to take thy] coat also.

textMismatch.clean: They said therefore unto him, What sign shewest thou then, that we may see, and believe thee? what dost thou work?
textMismatch.wharton: Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask [them] not again.

textMismatch.clean: Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.
textMismatch.wharton: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.

textMismatch.clean: Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.
textMismatch.wharton: For if ye love them which love you, what thank have ye? for sinners also love those that love them.

textMismatch.clean: For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.
textMismatch.wharton: And if ye do good to them which do good to you, what thank have ye? for sinners also do even the same.

textMismatch.clean: Then said they unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread.
textMismatch.wharton: And if ye lend [to them] of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.

textMismatch.clean: And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
textMismatch.wharton: But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and [to] the evil.

textMismatch.clean: But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not.
textMismatch.wharton: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.

textMismatch.clean: All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.
textMismatch.wharton: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven:

textMismatch.clean: For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.
textMismatch.wharton: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.

textMismatch.clean: And this is the Fathers will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.
textMismatch.wharton: And he spake a parable unto them, Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the ditch?

textMismatch.clean: And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.
textMismatch.wharton: The disciple is not above his master: but every one that is perfect shall be as his master.

textMismatch.clean: The Jews then murmured at him, because he said, I am the bread which came down from heaven.
textMismatch.wharton: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brothers eye, but perceivest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

textMismatch.clean: And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?
textMismatch.wharton: Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to pull out the mote that is in thy broth

textMismatch.clean: Jesus therefore answered and said unto them, Murmur not among yourselves.
textMismatch.wharton: For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

textMismatch.clean: No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day.
textMismatch.wharton: For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.

textMismatch.clean: It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me.
textMismatch.wharton: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.

textMismatch.clean: Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he which is of God, he hath seen the Father.
textMismatch.wharton: And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?

textMismatch.clean: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me hath everlasting life.
textMismatch.wharton: Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like:

textMismatch.clean: I am that bread of life.
textMismatch.wharton: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.

textMismatch.clean: Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead.
textMismatch.wharton: But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.

textMismatch.clean: AFTER these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Jewry, because the Jews sought to kill him.
textMismatch.wharton: Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.

textMismatch.clean: Now the Jews feast of tabernacles was at hand.
textMismatch.wharton: And a certain centurions servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.

textMismatch.clean: His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judæa, that thy disciples also may see the works that thou doest.
textMismatch.wharton: And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.

textMismatch.clean: For [there] [is] no man [that] doeth any thing in secret, and he himself seeketh to be known openly. If thou do these things, shew thyself to the world.
textMismatch.wharton: And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:

textMismatch.clean: For neither did his brethren believe in him.
textMismatch.wharton: For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.

textMismatch.clean: Then Jesus said unto them, My time is not yet come: but your time is alway ready.
textMismatch.wharton: Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:

textMismatch.clean: The world cannot hate you; but me it hateth, because I testify of it, that the works thereof are evil.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.

textMismatch.clean: Go ye up unto this feast: I go not up yet unto this feast; for my time is not yet full come.
textMismatch.wharton: For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth [it].

textMismatch.clean: When he had said these words unto them, he abode [still] in Galilee.
textMismatch.wharton: When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

textMismatch.clean: But when his brethren were gone up, then went he also up unto the feast, not openly, but as it were in secret.
textMismatch.wharton: And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole that had been sick.

textMismatch.clean: Then the Jews sought him at the feast, and said, Where is he?
textMismatch.wharton: And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people.

textMismatch.clean: And there was much murmuring among the people concerning him: for some said, He is a good man: others said, Nay; but he deceiveth the people.
textMismatch.wharton: Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.

textMismatch.clean: Howbeit no man spake openly of him for fear of the Jews.
textMismatch.wharton: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.

textMismatch.clean: Now about the midst of the feast Jesus went up into the temple, and taught.
textMismatch.wharton: And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare [him] stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.

textMismatch.clean: And the Jews marvelled, saying, How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?
textMismatch.wharton: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.

textMismatch.clean: Jesus answered them, and said, My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.
textMismatch.wharton: And there came a fear on all: and they glorified God, saying, That a great prophet is risen up among us; and, That God hath visited his people.

textMismatch.clean: If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or [whether] I speak of myself.
textMismatch.wharton: And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judaea, and throughout all the region round about.

textMismatch.clean: He that speaketh of himself seeketh his own glory: but he that seeketh his glory that sent him, the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.
textMismatch.wharton: And the disciples of John shewed him of all these things.

textMismatch.clean: Did not Moses give you the law, and [yet] none of you keepeth the law? Why go ye about to kill me?
textMismatch.wharton: And John calling [unto him] two of his disciples sent [them] to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?

textMismatch.clean: The people answered and said, Thou hast a devil: who goeth about to kill thee?
textMismatch.wharton: When the men were come unto him, they said, John Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?

textMismatch.clean: Jesus answered and said unto them, I have done one work, and ye all marvel.
textMismatch.wharton: And in that same hour he cured many of [their] infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; and unto many [that were] blind he gave sight.

textMismatch.clean: Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.
textMismatch.wharton: Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.

textMismatch.clean: If a man on the sabbath day receive circumcision, that the law of Moses should not be broken; are ye angry at me, because I have made a man every whit whole on the sabbath day?
textMismatch.wharton: And blessed is [he], whosoever shall not be offended in me.

textMismatch.clean: Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.
textMismatch.wharton: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak unto the people concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness for to see? A reed shaken with the wind?

textMismatch.clean: Then said some of them of Jerusalem, Is not this he, whom they seek to kill?
textMismatch.wharton: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they which are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings courts.

textMismatch.clean: But, lo, he speaketh boldly, and they say nothing unto him. Do the rulers know indeed that this is the very Christ?
textMismatch.wharton: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.

textMismatch.clean: Howbeit we know this man whence he is: but when Christ cometh, no man knoweth whence he is.
textMismatch.wharton: This is [he], of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.

textMismatch.clean: Then cried Jesus in the temple as he taught, saying, Ye both know me, and ye know whence I am: and I am not come of myself, but he that sent me is true, whom ye know not.
textMismatch.wharton: For I say unto you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.

textMismatch.clean: But I know him: for I am from him, and he hath sent me.
textMismatch.wharton: And all the people that heard [him], and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.

textMismatch.clean: Then they sought to take him: but no man laid hands on him, because his hour was not yet come.
textMismatch.wharton: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.

textMismatch.clean: And many of the people believed on him, and said, When Christ cometh, will he do more miracles than these which this [man] hath done?
textMismatch.wharton: And the Lord said, Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?

textMismatch.clean: The Pharisees heard that the people murmured such things concerning him; and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers to take him.
textMismatch.wharton: They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.

textMismatch.clean: Then said Jesus unto them, Yet a little while am I with you, and [then] I go unto him that sent me.
textMismatch.wharton: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a devil.

textMismatch.clean: Ye shall seek me, and shall not find [me:] and where I am, [thither] ye cannot come.
textMismatch.wharton: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners!

textMismatch.clean: Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?
