textMismatch.clean: But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such [cases:] but God hath called us to peace.
textMismatch.wharton: For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.

textMismatch.clean: For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save [thy] husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save [thy] wife?
textMismatch.wharton: If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that [it is] good.

textMismatch.clean: But as God hath distributed to every man, as the Lord hath called every one, so let him walk. And so ordain I in all churches.
textMismatch.wharton: Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.

textMismatch.clean: Is any man called being circumcised? let him not become uncircumcised. Is any called in uncircumcision? let him not be circumcised.
textMismatch.wharton: For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but [how] to perform that which is good I find not.

textMismatch.clean: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God.
textMismatch.wharton: For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.

textMismatch.clean: Let every man abide in the same calling wherein he was called.
textMismatch.wharton: Now if I do that I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.

textMismatch.clean: Art thou called [being] a servant? care not for it: but if thou mayest be made free, use [it] rather.
textMismatch.wharton: I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me.

textMismatch.clean: For he that is called in the Lord, [being] a servant, is the Lords freeman: likewise also he that is called, [being] free, is Christs servant.
textMismatch.wharton: For I delight in the law of God after the inward man:

textMismatch.clean: Ye are bought with a price; be not ye the servants of men.
textMismatch.wharton: But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.

textMismatch.clean: Brethren, let every man, wherein he is called, therein abide with God.
textMismatch.wharton: O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?

textMismatch.clean: Now concerning virgins I have no commandment of the Lord: yet I give my judgment, as one that hath obtained mercy of the Lord to be faithful.
textMismatch.wharton: I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.

textMismatch.clean: NOW as touching things offered unto idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.
textMismatch.wharton: [There is] therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

textMismatch.clean: And if any man think that he knoweth any thing, he knoweth nothing yet as he ought to know.
textMismatch.wharton: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death.

textMismatch.clean: But if any man love God, the same is known of him.
textMismatch.wharton: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:

textMismatch.clean: As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol [is] nothing in the world, and that [there] [is] none other God but one.
textMismatch.wharton: That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

textMismatch.clean: For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,)
textMismatch.wharton: For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit.

textMismatch.clean: But to us [there] [is] [but] one God, the Father, of whom [are] all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom [are] all things, and we by him.
textMismatch.wharton: For to be carnally minded [is] death; but to be spiritually minded [is] life and peace.

textMismatch.clean: Howbeit [there] [is] not in every man that knowledge: for some with conscience of the idol unto this hour eat [it] as a thing offered unto an idol; and their conscience being weak is defiled.
textMismatch.wharton: Because the carnal mind [is] enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be.

textMismatch.clean: But meat commendeth us not to God: for neither, if we eat, are we the better; neither, if we eat not, are we the worse.
textMismatch.wharton: So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.

textMismatch.clean: But take heed lest by any means this liberty of yours become a stumblingblock to them that are weak.
textMismatch.wharton: But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.

textMismatch.clean: For if any man see thee which hast knowledge sit at meat in the idols temple, shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols;
textMismatch.wharton: And if Christ [be] in you, the body [is] dead because of sin; but the Spirit [is] life because of righteousness.

textMismatch.clean: And through thy knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ died?
textMismatch.wharton: But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you.

textMismatch.clean: But when ye sin so against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, ye sin against Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore, if meat make my brother to offend, I will eat no flesh while the world standeth, lest I make my brother to offend.
textMismatch.wharton: For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live.

textMismatch.clean: AM I not an apostle? am I not free? have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? are not ye my work in the Lord?
textMismatch.wharton: I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Ghost,

textMismatch.clean: If I be not an apostle unto others, yet doubtless I am to you: for the seal of mine apostleship are ye in the Lord.
textMismatch.wharton: That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart.

textMismatch.clean: Mine answer to them that do examine me is this,
textMismatch.wharton: For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh:

textMismatch.clean: Have we not power to eat and to drink?
textMismatch.wharton: Who are Israelites; to whom [pertaineth] the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service [of God], and the promises;

textMismatch.clean: Have we not power to lead about a sister, a wife, as well as other apostles, and [as] the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?
textMismatch.wharton: Whose [are] the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ [came], who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.

textMismatch.clean: Or I only and Barnabas, have not we power to forbear working?
textMismatch.wharton: Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they [are] not all Israel, which are of Israel:

textMismatch.clean: Who goeth a warfare any time at his own charges? who planteth a vineyard, and eateth not of the fruit thereof? or who feedeth a flock, and eateth not of the milk of the flock?
textMismatch.wharton: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, [are they] all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.

textMismatch.clean: Say I these things as a man? or saith not the law the same also?
textMismatch.wharton: That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these [are] not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

textMismatch.clean: For it is written in the law of Moses, Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treadeth out the corn. Doth God take care for oxen?
textMismatch.wharton: For this [is] the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sara shall have a son.

textMismatch.clean: Or saith he [it] altogether for our sakes? For our sakes, no doubt, [this] is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope; and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.
textMismatch.wharton: And not only [this]; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, [even] by our father Isaac;

textMismatch.clean: If we have sown unto you spiritual things, [is] [it] a great thing if we shall reap your carnal things?
textMismatch.wharton: (For [the children] being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;)

textMismatch.clean: If others be partakers of [this] power over you, [are] not we rather? Nevertheless we have not used this power; but suffer all things, lest we should hinder the gospel of Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger.

textMismatch.clean: Do ye not know that they which minister about holy things live [of] [the] [things] of the temple? and they which wait at the altar are partakers with the altar?
textMismatch.wharton: As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.

textMismatch.clean: Even so hath the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel.
textMismatch.wharton: What shall we say then? [Is there] unrighteousness with God? God forbid.

textMismatch.clean: But I have used none of these things: neither have I written these things, that it should be so done unto me: for [it] [were] better for me to die, than that any man should make my glorying void.
textMismatch.wharton: For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.

textMismatch.clean: For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!
textMismatch.wharton: So then [it is] not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.

textMismatch.clean: For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation [of] [the] [gospel] is committed unto me.
textMismatch.wharton: For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.

textMismatch.clean: What is my reward then? [Verily] that, when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel of Christ without charge, that I abuse not my power in the gospel.
textMismatch.wharton: Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will [have mercy], and whom he will he hardeneth.

textMismatch.clean: For though I be free from all [men], yet have I made myself servant unto all, that I might gain the more.
textMismatch.wharton: Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will?

textMismatch.clean: And unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; to them that are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain them that are under the law;
textMismatch.wharton: Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed [it], Why hast thou made me thus?

textMismatch.clean: To them that are without law, as without law, (being not without law to God, but under the law to Christ,) that I might gain them that are without law.
textMismatch.wharton: Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?

textMismatch.clean: To the weak became I as weak, that I might gain the weak: I am made all things to all [men], that I might by all means save some.
textMismatch.wharton: [What] if God, willing to shew [his] wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction:

textMismatch.clean: And this I do for the gospels sake, that I might be partaker thereof with [you].
textMismatch.wharton: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory,

textMismatch.clean: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.
textMismatch.wharton: Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?

textMismatch.clean: And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they [do] [it] to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.
textMismatch.wharton: As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.

textMismatch.clean: I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air:
textMismatch.wharton: And it shall come to pass, [that] in the place where it was said unto them, Ye [are] not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.

textMismatch.clean: But I keep under my body, and bring [it] into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.
textMismatch.wharton: Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved:

textMismatch.clean: MOREOVER, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;
textMismatch.wharton: Brethren, my hearts desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.

textMismatch.clean: And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
textMismatch.wharton: For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.

textMismatch.clean: And did all eat the same spiritual meat;
textMismatch.wharton: For they being ignorant of Gods righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.

textMismatch.clean: And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: For Christ [is] the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.

textMismatch.clean: But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.
textMismatch.wharton: For Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them.

textMismatch.clean: Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.
textMismatch.wharton: But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down [from above]:)

textMismatch.clean: Neither be ye idolaters, as [were] some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.
textMismatch.wharton: Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.)

textMismatch.clean: Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.
textMismatch.wharton: But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, [even] in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach;

textMismatch.clean: Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.
textMismatch.wharton: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.

textMismatch.clean: Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.
textMismatch.wharton: For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

textMismatch.clean: Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.
textMismatch.wharton: For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.
textMismatch.wharton: For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him.

textMismatch.clean: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God [is] faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear [it].
textMismatch.wharton: For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.
textMismatch.wharton: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?

textMismatch.clean: I speak as to wise men; judge ye what I say.
textMismatch.wharton: And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!

textMismatch.clean: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?
textMismatch.wharton: But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?

textMismatch.clean: For we [being] many are one bread, [and] one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.
textMismatch.wharton: So then faith [cometh] by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

textMismatch.clean: Behold Israel after the flesh: are not they which eat of the sacrifices partakers of the altar?
textMismatch.wharton: But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.

textMismatch.clean: What say I then? that the idol is any thing, or that which is offered in sacrifice to idols is any thing?
textMismatch.wharton: But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by [them that are] no people, [and] by a foolish nation I will anger you.

textMismatch.clean: But [I] [say], that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God: and I would not that ye should have fellowship with devils.
textMismatch.wharton: But Esaias is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me.

textMismatch.clean: Ye cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils: ye cannot be partakers of the Lords table, and of the table of devils.
textMismatch.wharton: But to Israel he saith, All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.

textMismatch.clean: BE ye followers of me, even as I also [am] of Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, [of] the tribe of Benjamin.

textMismatch.clean: Now I praise you, brethren, that ye remember me in all things, and keep the ordinances, as I delivered [them] to you.
textMismatch.wharton: God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel, saying,

textMismatch.clean: But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman [is] the man; and the head of Christ [is] God.
textMismatch.wharton: Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.

textMismatch.clean: Every man praying or prophesying, having [his] head covered, dishonoureth his head.
textMismatch.wharton: But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to [the image of] Baal.

textMismatch.clean: But every woman that prayeth or prophesieth with [her] head uncovered dishonoureth her head: for that is even all one as if she were shaven.
textMismatch.wharton: Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

textMismatch.clean: For if the woman be not covered, let her also be shorn: but if it be a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered.
textMismatch.wharton: And if by grace, then [is it] no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if [it be] of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.

textMismatch.clean: For a man indeed ought not to cover [his] head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.
textMismatch.wharton: What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded

textMismatch.clean: For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.
textMismatch.wharton: (According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.

textMismatch.clean: Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.
textMismatch.wharton: And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them:

textMismatch.clean: For this cause ought the woman to have power on [her] head because of the angels.
textMismatch.wharton: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway.

textMismatch.clean: Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord.
textMismatch.wharton: I say then, Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid: but [rather] through their fall salvation [is come] unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy.

textMismatch.clean: For as the woman [is] of the man, even so [is] the man also by the woman; but all things of God.
textMismatch.wharton: Now if the fall of them [be] the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness?

textMismatch.clean: Judge in yourselves: is it comely that a woman pray unto God uncovered?
textMismatch.wharton: For I speak to you Gentiles, inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify mine office:

textMismatch.clean: Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him?
textMismatch.wharton: If by any means I may provoke to emulation [them which are] my flesh, and might save some of them.

textMismatch.clean: But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for [her] hair is given her for a covering.
textMismatch.wharton: For if the casting away of them [be] the reconciling of the world, what [shall] the receiving [of them be], but life from the dead?

textMismatch.clean: But if any man seem to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither the churches of God.
textMismatch.wharton: For if the firstfruit [be] holy, the lump [is] also [holy]: and if the root [be] holy, so [are] the branches.

textMismatch.clean: Now in this that I declare [unto] [you] I praise [you] not, that ye come together not for the better, but for the worse.
textMismatch.wharton: And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree;

textMismatch.clean: For first of all, when ye come together in the church, I hear that there be divisions among you; and I partly believe it.
textMismatch.wharton: Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.

textMismatch.clean: For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.
textMismatch.wharton: Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in.

textMismatch.clean: When ye come together therefore into one place, [this] is not to eat the Lords supper.
textMismatch.wharton: Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear:

textMismatch.clean: For in eating every one taketh before [other] his own supper: and one is hungry, and another is drunken.
textMismatch.wharton: For if God spared not the natural branches, [take heed] lest he also spare not thee.

textMismatch.clean: What? have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise ye the church of God, and shame them that have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I praise [you] not.
textMismatch.wharton: Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in [his] goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.

textMismatch.clean: For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, That the Lord Jesus the [same] night in which he was betrayed took bread:
textMismatch.wharton: And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be graffed in: for God is able to graff them in again.

textMismatch.clean: And when he had given thanks, he brake [it], and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.
textMismatch.wharton: For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert graffed contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural [branches], be graffed into their own olive tree?

textMismatch.clean: After the same manner also [he] [took] the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink [it], in remembrance of me.
textMismatch.wharton: For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.

textMismatch.clean: For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lords death till he come.
textMismatch.wharton: And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob:

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore whosoever shall eat this bread, and drink [this] cup of the Lord, unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
textMismatch.wharton: For this [is] my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.

textMismatch.clean: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of [that] bread, and drink of [that] cup.
textMismatch.wharton: As concerning the gospel, [they are] enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, [they are] beloved for the fathers sakes.

textMismatch.clean: For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lords body.
textMismatch.wharton: For the gifts and calling of God [are] without repentance.

textMismatch.clean: For this cause many [are] weak and sickly among you, and many sleep.
textMismatch.wharton: For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief:

textMismatch.clean: For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.
textMismatch.wharton: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy.

textMismatch.clean: But when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world.
textMismatch.wharton: For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore, my brethren, when ye come together to eat, tarry one for another.
textMismatch.wharton: O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable [are] his judgments, and his ways past finding out!

textMismatch.clean: And if any man hunger, let him eat at home; that ye come not together unto condemnation. And the rest will I set in order when I come.
textMismatch.wharton: For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counseller?

textMismatch.clean: NOW concerning spiritual [gifts], brethren, I would not have you ignorant.
textMismatch.wharton: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, [which is] your reasonable service.

textMismatch.clean: Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.
textMismatch.wharton: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what [is] that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and [that] no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost.
textMismatch.wharton: For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think [of himself] more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.

textMismatch.clean: Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit.
textMismatch.wharton: For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office:

textMismatch.clean: And there are differences of administrations, but the same Lord.
textMismatch.wharton: So we, [being] many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.

textMismatch.clean: And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all.
textMismatch.wharton: Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, [let us prophesy] according to the proportion of faith;

textMismatch.clean: But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.
textMismatch.wharton: Or ministry, [let us wait] on [our] ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching;

textMismatch.clean: For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit;
textMismatch.wharton: Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, [let him do it] with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.

textMismatch.clean: To another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit;
textMismatch.wharton: [Let] love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.

textMismatch.clean: To another the working of miracles; to another prophecy; to another discerning of spirits; to another [divers] kinds of tongues; to another the interpretation of tongues:
textMismatch.wharton: [Be] kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another;

textMismatch.clean: But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will.
textMismatch.wharton: Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;

textMismatch.clean: For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also [is] Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;

textMismatch.clean: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether [we] [be] Jews or Gentiles, whether [we] [be] bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit.
textMismatch.wharton: Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality.

textMismatch.clean: For the body is not one member, but many.
textMismatch.wharton: Bless them which persecute you: bless, and curse not.

textMismatch.clean: If the foot shall say, Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?
textMismatch.wharton: Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.

textMismatch.clean: And if the ear shall say, Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?
textMismatch.wharton: [Be] of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.

textMismatch.clean: If the whole body [were] an eye, where [were] the hearing? If the whole [were] hearing, where [were] the smelling?
textMismatch.wharton: Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men.

textMismatch.clean: But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.
textMismatch.wharton: If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.

textMismatch.clean: And if they were all one member, where [were] the body?
textMismatch.wharton: Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but [rather] give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance [is] mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.

textMismatch.clean: But now [are] [they] many members, yet but one body.
textMismatch.wharton: Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.

textMismatch.clean: And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.
textMismatch.wharton: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

textMismatch.clean: THOUGH I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become [as] sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.
textMismatch.wharton: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.

textMismatch.clean: And though I have [the] [gift] [of] prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing.
textMismatch.wharton: Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.

textMismatch.clean: And though I bestow all my goods to feed [the] [poor], and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.
textMismatch.wharton: For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same:

textMismatch.clean: Charity suffereth long, [and] is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,
textMismatch.wharton: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to [execute] wrath upon him that doeth evil.

textMismatch.clean: Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore [ye] must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake.

textMismatch.clean: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth;
textMismatch.wharton: For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are Gods ministers, attending continually upon this very thing.

textMismatch.clean: Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.
textMismatch.wharton: Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute [is due]; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.

textMismatch.clean: Charity never faileth: but whether [there] [be] prophecies, they shall fail; whether [there] [be] tongues, they shall cease; whether [there] [be] knowledge, it shall vanish away.
textMismatch.wharton: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.

textMismatch.clean: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.
textMismatch.wharton: For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet; and if [there be] any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

textMismatch.clean: But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away.
textMismatch.wharton: Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love [is] the fulfilling of the law.

textMismatch.clean: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.
textMismatch.wharton: And that, knowing the time, that now [it is] high time to awake out of sleep: for now [is] our salvation nearer than when we believed.

textMismatch.clean: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.
textMismatch.wharton: The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light.

textMismatch.clean: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these [is] charity.
textMismatch.wharton: Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envying.

textMismatch.clean: FOLLOW after charity, and desire spiritual [gifts], but rather that ye may prophesy.
textMismatch.wharton: Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, [but] not to doubtful disputations.

textMismatch.clean: For he that speaketh in an [unknown] tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth [him;] howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries.
textMismatch.wharton: For one believeth that he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eateth herbs.

textMismatch.clean: But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men [to] edification, and exhortation, and comfort.
textMismatch.wharton: Let not him that eateth despise him that eateth not; and let not him which eateth not judge him that eateth: for God hath received him.

textMismatch.clean: He that speaketh in an [unknown] tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.
textMismatch.wharton: Who art thou that judgest another mans servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.

textMismatch.clean: I would that ye all spake with tongues, but rather that ye prophesied: for greater [is] he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.
textMismatch.wharton: One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day [alike]. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.

textMismatch.clean: Now, brethren, if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, except I shall speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophesying, or by doctrine?
textMismatch.wharton: He that regardeth the day, regardeth [it] unto the Lord; and he that regardeth not the day, to the Lord he doth not regard [it]. He that eateth, eateth to the Lord, for he giveth God thanks; and he that eateth not, to the Lord he eateth not, and giveth God thanks.

textMismatch.clean: And even things without life giving sound, whether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped?
textMismatch.wharton: For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself.

textMismatch.clean: For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?
textMismatch.wharton: For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lords.

textMismatch.clean: So likewise ye, except ye utter by the tongue words easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? for ye shall speak into the air.
textMismatch.wharton: For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living.

textMismatch.clean: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them [is] without signification.
textMismatch.wharton: But why dost thou judge thy brother? or why dost thou set at nought thy brother? for we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.

textMismatch.clean: Therefore if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh [shall] [be] a barbarian unto me.
textMismatch.wharton: For it is written, [As] I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.

textMismatch.clean: Even so ye, forasmuch as ye are zealous of spiritual [gifts], seek that ye may excel to the edifying of the church.
textMismatch.wharton: So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore let him that speaketh in an [unknown] tongue pray that he may interpret.
textMismatch.wharton: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in [his] brothers way.

textMismatch.clean: For if I pray in an [unknown] tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.
textMismatch.wharton: I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that [there is] nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him [it is] unclean.

textMismatch.clean: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also: I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.
textMismatch.wharton: But if thy brother be grieved with [thy] meat, now walkest thou not charitably. Destroy not him with thy meat, for whom Christ died.

textMismatch.clean: Else when thou shalt bless with the spirit, how shall he that occupieth the room of the unlearned say Amen at thy giving of thanks, seeing he understandeth not what thou sayest?
textMismatch.wharton: Let not then your good be evil spoken of:

textMismatch.clean: For thou verily givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.
textMismatch.wharton: For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink; but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.

textMismatch.clean: I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than ye all:
textMismatch.wharton: For he that in these things serveth Christ [is] acceptable to God, and approved of men.

textMismatch.clean: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that [by] [my] [voice] I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an [unknown] tongue.
textMismatch.wharton: Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another.

textMismatch.clean: Brethren, be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men.
textMismatch.wharton: For meat destroy not the work of God. All things indeed [are] pure; but [it is] evil for that man who eateth with offence.

textMismatch.clean: In the law it is written, With [men] [of] other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the Lord.
textMismatch.wharton: [It is] good neither to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor [any thing] whereby thy brother stumbleth, or is offended, or is made weak.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying [serveth] not for them that believe not, but for them which believe.
textMismatch.wharton: Hast thou faith? have [it] to thyself before God. Happy [is] he that condemneth not himself in that thing which he alloweth.

textMismatch.clean: If therefore the whole church be come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in [those] [that] [are] unlearned, or unbelievers, will they not say that ye are mad?
textMismatch.wharton: And he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because [he eateth] not of faith: for whatsoever [is] not of faith is sin.

textMismatch.clean: MOREOVER, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand;
textMismatch.wharton: We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

textMismatch.clean: By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain.
textMismatch.wharton: Let every one of us please [his] neighbour for [his] good to edification.

textMismatch.clean: For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;
textMismatch.wharton: For even Christ pleased not himself; but, as it is written, The reproaches of them that reproached thee fell on me.

textMismatch.clean: And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:
textMismatch.wharton: For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

textMismatch.clean: And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve:
textMismatch.wharton: Now the God of patience and consolation grant you to be likeminded one toward another according to Christ Jesus:

textMismatch.clean: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep.
textMismatch.wharton: That ye may with one mind [and] one mouth glorify God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

textMismatch.clean: After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore receive ye one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God.

textMismatch.clean: And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.
textMismatch.wharton: Now I say that Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises [made] unto the fathers:

textMismatch.clean: For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
textMismatch.wharton: And that the Gentiles might glorify God for [his] mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name.

textMismatch.clean: But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which [was] [bestowed] upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
textMismatch.wharton: And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people.

textMismatch.clean: Therefore whether [it] [were] I or they, so we preach, and so ye believed.
textMismatch.wharton: And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people.

textMismatch.clean: Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead?
textMismatch.wharton: And again, Esaias saith, There shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise to reign over the Gentiles; in him shall the Gentiles trust.

textMismatch.clean: But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen:
textMismatch.wharton: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.

textMismatch.clean: And if Christ be not risen, then [is] our preaching vain, and your faith [is] also vain.
textMismatch.wharton: And I myself also am persuaded of you, my brethren, that ye also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.

textMismatch.clean: Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God; because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead rise not.
textMismatch.wharton: Nevertheless, brethren, I have written the more boldly unto you in some sort, as putting you in mind, because of the grace that is given to me of God,

textMismatch.clean: For if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised:
textMismatch.wharton: That I should be the minister of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles, ministering the gospel of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be acceptable, being sanctified by the Holy Ghost.

textMismatch.clean: And if Christ be not raised, your faith [is] vain; ye are yet in your sins.
textMismatch.wharton: I have therefore whereof I may glory through Jesus Christ in those things which pertain to God.

textMismatch.clean: Then they also which are fallen asleep in Christ are perished.
textMismatch.wharton: For I will not dare to speak of any of those things which Christ hath not wrought by me, to make the Gentiles obedient, by word and deed,

textMismatch.clean: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.
textMismatch.wharton: Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God; so that from Jerusalem, and round about unto Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ.

textMismatch.clean: But now is Christ risen from the dead, [and] become the firstfruits of them that slept.
textMismatch.wharton: Yea, so have I strived to preach the gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another mans foundation:

textMismatch.clean: For since by man [came] death, by man [came] also the resurrection of the dead.
textMismatch.wharton: But as it is written, To whom he was not spoken of, they shall see: and they that have not heard shall understand.

textMismatch.clean: For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.
textMismatch.wharton: For which cause also I have been much hindered from coming to you.

textMismatch.clean: But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christs at his coming.
textMismatch.wharton: But now having no more place in these parts, and having a great desire these many years to come unto you;

textMismatch.clean: Then [cometh] the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power.
textMismatch.wharton: Whensoever I take my journey into Spain, I will come to you: for I trust to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my way thitherward by you, if first I be somewhat filled with your [company].

textMismatch.clean: For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet.
textMismatch.wharton: But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints.

textMismatch.clean: The last enemy [that] shall be destroyed [is] death.
textMismatch.wharton: For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem.

textMismatch.clean: For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith, all things are put under [him], [it] [is] manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him.
textMismatch.wharton: It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things.

textMismatch.clean: And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.
textMismatch.wharton: When therefore I have performed this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will come by you into Spain.

textMismatch.clean: Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?
textMismatch.wharton: And I am sure that, when I come unto you, I shall come in the fulness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ.

textMismatch.clean: And why stand we in jeopardy every hour?
textMismatch.wharton: Now I beseech you, brethren, for the Lord Jesus Christs sake, and for the love of the Spirit, that ye strive together with me in [your] prayers to God for me;

textMismatch.clean: I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.
textMismatch.wharton: That I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judaea; and that my service which [I have] for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints;

textMismatch.clean: If after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantageth it me, if the dead rise not? let us eat and drink; for to morrow we die.
textMismatch.wharton: That I may come unto you with joy by the will of God, and may with you be refreshed.

textMismatch.clean: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.
textMismatch.wharton: Now the God of peace [be] with you all. Amen.

textMismatch.clean: NOW concerning the collection for the saints, as I have given order to the churches of Galatia, even so do ye.
textMismatch.wharton: I commend unto you Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea:

textMismatch.clean: Upon the first [day] of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as [God] hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come.
textMismatch.wharton: That ye receive her in the Lord, as becometh saints, and that ye assist her in whatsoever business she hath need of you: for she hath been a succourer of many, and of myself also.

textMismatch.clean: And when I come, whomsoever ye shall approve by [your] letters, them will I send to bring your liberality unto Jerusalem.
textMismatch.wharton: Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus:

textMismatch.clean: And if it be meet that I go also, they shall go with me.
textMismatch.wharton: Who have for my life laid down their own necks: unto whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.

textMismatch.clean: Now I will come unto you, when I shall pass through Macedonia: for I do pass through Macedonia.
textMismatch.wharton: Likewise [greet] the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epaenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.

textMismatch.clean: And it may be that I will abide, yea, and winter with you, that ye may bring me on my journey whithersoever I go.
textMismatch.wharton: Greet Mary, who bestowed much labour on us.

textMismatch.clean: For I will not see you now by the way; but I trust to tarry a while with you, if the Lord permit.
textMismatch.wharton: Salute Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen, and my fellowprisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.

textMismatch.clean: But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost.
textMismatch.wharton: Greet Amplias my beloved in the Lord.

textMismatch.clean: For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and [there] [are] many adversaries.
textMismatch.wharton: Salute Urbane, our helper in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.

textMismatch.clean: Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also [do].
textMismatch.wharton: Salute Apelles approved in Christ. Salute them which are of Aristobulus [household].

textMismatch.clean: Let no man therefore despise him: but conduct him forth in peace, that he may come unto me: for I look for him with the brethren.
textMismatch.wharton: Salute Herodion my kinsman. Greet them that be of the [household] of Narcissus, which are in the Lord.

textMismatch.clean: As touching [our] brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time.
textMismatch.wharton: Salute Tryphena and Tryphosa, who labour in the Lord. Salute the beloved Persis, which laboured much in the Lord.

textMismatch.clean: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.
textMismatch.wharton: Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

textMismatch.clean: Let all your things be done with charity.
textMismatch.wharton: Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren which are with them.

textMismatch.clean: I beseech you, brethren, (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and [that] they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints,)
textMismatch.wharton: Salute Philologus, and Julia, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints which are with them.

textMismatch.clean: That ye submit yourselves unto such, and to every one that helpeth with [us], and laboureth.
textMismatch.wharton: Salute one another with an holy kiss. The churches of Christ salute you.

textMismatch.clean: I am glad of the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus: for that which was lacking on your part they have supplied.
textMismatch.wharton: Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.

textMismatch.clean: For they have refreshed my spirit and yours: therefore acknowledge ye them that are such.
textMismatch.wharton: For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.

textMismatch.clean: The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house.
textMismatch.wharton: For your obedience is come abroad unto all [men]. I am glad therefore on your behalf: but yet I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil.

textMismatch.clean: All the brethren greet you. Greet ye one another with an holy kiss.
textMismatch.wharton: And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you. Amen.

textMismatch.clean: The salutation of [me] Paul with mine own hand.
textMismatch.wharton: Timotheus my workfellow, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen, salute you.

textMismatch.clean: If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maran-atha.
textMismatch.wharton: I Tertius, who wrote [this] epistle, salute you in the Lord.

textMismatch.clean: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you.
textMismatch.wharton: Gaius mine host, and of the whole church, saluteth you. Erastus the chamberlain of the city saluteth you, and Quartus a brother.

textMismatch.clean: My love [be] with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
textMismatch.wharton: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen.

textMismatch.clean: PAUL, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy [our] brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia:
textMismatch.wharton: Paul, called [to be] an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes [our] brother,

textMismatch.clean: Grace [be] to you and peace from God our Father, and [from] the Lord Jesus Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called [to be] saints, with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both theirs and ours:

textMismatch.clean: Blessed [be] God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;
textMismatch.wharton: Grace [be] unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and [from] the Lord Jesus Christ.

textMismatch.clean: Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.
textMismatch.wharton: I thank my God always on your behalf, for the grace of God which is given you by Jesus Christ;

textMismatch.clean: For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: That in every thing ye are enriched by him, in all utterance, and [in] all knowledge;

textMismatch.clean: And whether we be afflicted, [it] [is] for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer: or whether we be comforted, [it] [is] for your consolation and salvation.
textMismatch.wharton: Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you:

textMismatch.clean: And our hope of you [is] stedfast, knowing, that as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so [shall] [ye] [be] also of the consolation.
textMismatch.wharton: So that ye come behind in no gift; waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ:

textMismatch.clean: For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life:
textMismatch.wharton: Who shall also confirm you unto the end, [that ye may be] blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

textMismatch.clean: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead:
textMismatch.wharton: God [is] faithful, by whom ye were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

textMismatch.clean: Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver [us;]
textMismatch.wharton: Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and [that] there be no divisions among you; but [that] ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.

textMismatch.clean: Ye also helping together by prayer for us, that for the gift [bestowed] upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf.
textMismatch.wharton: For it hath been declared unto me of you, my brethren, by them [which are of the house] of Chloe, that there are contentions among you.

textMismatch.clean: For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward.
textMismatch.wharton: Now this I say, that every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ.

textMismatch.clean: For we write none other things unto you, than what ye read or acknowledge; and I trust ye shall acknowledge even to the end;
textMismatch.wharton: Is Christ divided? was Paul crucified for you? or were ye baptized in the name of Paul?

textMismatch.clean: As also ye have acknowledged us in part, that we are your rejoicing, even as ye also [are] ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.
textMismatch.wharton: I thank God that I baptized none of you, but Crispus and Gaius;

textMismatch.clean: And in this confidence I was minded to come unto you before, that ye might have a second benefit;
textMismatch.wharton: Lest any should say that I had baptized in mine own name.

textMismatch.clean: And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judæa.
textMismatch.wharton: And I baptized also the household of Stephanas: besides, I know not whether I baptized any other.

textMismatch.clean: When I therefore was thus minded, did I use lightness? or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be yea yea, and nay nay?
textMismatch.wharton: For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel: not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect.

textMismatch.clean: But [as] God [is] true, our word toward you was not yea and nay.
textMismatch.wharton: For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God.

textMismatch.clean: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, [even] by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea.
textMismatch.wharton: For it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent.

textMismatch.clean: For all the promises of God in him [are] yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.
textMismatch.wharton: Where [is] the wise? where [is] the scribe? where [is] the disputer of this world? hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?

textMismatch.clean: Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, [is] God;
textMismatch.wharton: For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.

textMismatch.clean: Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.
textMismatch.wharton: For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom:

textMismatch.clean: Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth.
textMismatch.wharton: But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness;

textMismatch.clean: Not for that we have dominion over your faith, but are helpers of your joy: for by faith ye stand.
textMismatch.wharton: But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.

textMismatch.clean: BUT I determined this with myself, that I would not come again to you in heaviness.
textMismatch.wharton: And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of God.

textMismatch.clean: For if I make you sorry, who is he then that maketh me glad, but the same which is made sorry by me?
textMismatch.wharton: For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

textMismatch.clean: And I wrote this same unto you, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy is [the] [joy] of you all.
textMismatch.wharton: And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.

textMismatch.clean: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears; not that ye should be grieved, but that ye might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you.
textMismatch.wharton: And my speech and my preaching [was] not with enticing words of mans wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power:

textMismatch.clean: But if any have caused grief, he hath not grieved me, but in part: that I may not overcharge you all.
textMismatch.wharton: That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.

textMismatch.clean: Sufficient to such a man [is] this punishment, which [was] [inflicted] of many.
textMismatch.wharton: Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought:

textMismatch.clean: So that contrariwise ye [ought] rather to forgive [him], and comfort [him], lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.
textMismatch.wharton: But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, [even] the hidden [wisdom], which God ordained before the world unto our glory:

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm [your] love toward him.
textMismatch.wharton: Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known [it], they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

textMismatch.clean: For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.
textMismatch.wharton: But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.

textMismatch.clean: To whom ye forgive any thing, I [forgive] also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I forgave [it], for your sakes [forgave] [I] [it] in the person of Christ;
textMismatch.wharton: But God hath revealed [them] unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.

textMismatch.clean: Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.
textMismatch.wharton: For what man knoweth the things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him? even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God.

textMismatch.clean: Furthermore, when I came to Troas to [preach] Christs gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord,
textMismatch.wharton: Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God.

textMismatch.clean: I had no rest in my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother: but taking my leave of them, I went from thence into Macedonia.
textMismatch.wharton: Which things also we speak, not in the words which mans wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

textMismatch.clean: Now thanks [be] unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.
textMismatch.wharton: But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know [them], because they are spiritually discerned.

textMismatch.clean: For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish:
textMismatch.wharton: But he that is spiritual judgeth all things, yet he himself is judged of no man.

textMismatch.clean: To the one [we] [are] the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who [is] sufficient for these things?
textMismatch.wharton: For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ.

textMismatch.clean: DO we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some [others], epistles of commendation to you, or [letters] of commendation from you?
textMismatch.wharton: And I, brethren, could not speak unto you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal, [even] as unto babes in Christ.

textMismatch.clean: Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men:
textMismatch.wharton: I have fed you with milk, and not with meat: for hitherto ye were not able [to bear it], neither yet now are ye able.

textMismatch.clean: [Forasmuch] [as] [ye] [are] manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.
textMismatch.wharton: For ye are yet carnal: for whereas [there is] among you envying, and strife, and divisions, are ye not carnal, and walk as men?

textMismatch.clean: And such trust have we through Christ to God-ward:
textMismatch.wharton: For while one saith, I am of Paul; and another, I [am] of Apollos; are ye not carnal?

textMismatch.clean: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency [is] of God;
textMismatch.wharton: Who then is Paul, and who [is] Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed, even as the Lord gave to every man?

textMismatch.clean: Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.
textMismatch.wharton: I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.

textMismatch.clean: But if the ministration of death, written [and] engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which [glory] was to be done away:
textMismatch.wharton: So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.

textMismatch.clean: How shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious?
textMismatch.wharton: Now he that planteth and he that watereth are one: and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour.

textMismatch.clean: For if the ministration of condemnation [be] glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.
textMismatch.wharton: For we are labourers together with God: ye are Gods husbandry, [ye are] Gods building.

textMismatch.clean: For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth.
textMismatch.wharton: According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon.

textMismatch.clean: For if that which is done away [was] glorious, much more that which remaineth [is] glorious.
textMismatch.wharton: For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

textMismatch.clean: Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech:
textMismatch.wharton: Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble;

textMismatch.clean: And not as Moses, [which] put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:
textMismatch.wharton: Every mans work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every mans work of what sort it is.

textMismatch.clean: But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which [vail] is done away in Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: If any mans work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward.

textMismatch.clean: But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart.
textMismatch.wharton: If any mans work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.

textMismatch.clean: Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.
textMismatch.wharton: Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and [that] the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?

textMismatch.clean: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord [is], there [is] liberty.
textMismatch.wharton: If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which [temple] ye are.

textMismatch.clean: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, [even] as by the Spirit of the Lord.
textMismatch.wharton: Let no man deceive himself. If any man among you seemeth to be wise in this world, let him become a fool, that he may be wise.

textMismatch.clean: THEREFORE seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not;
textMismatch.wharton: Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God.

textMismatch.clean: But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every mans conscience in the sight of God.
textMismatch.wharton: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.

textMismatch.clean: But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost:
textMismatch.wharton: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of mans judgment: yea, I judge not mine own self.

textMismatch.clean: In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.
textMismatch.wharton: For I know nothing by myself; yet am I not hereby justified: but he that judgeth me is the Lord.

textMismatch.clean: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus sake.
textMismatch.wharton: Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts: and then shall every man have praise of God.

textMismatch.clean: For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to [give] the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: And these things, brethren, I have in a figure transferred to myself and [to] Apollos for your sakes; that ye might learn in us not to think [of men] above that which is written, that no one of you be puffed up for one against another.

textMismatch.clean: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.
textMismatch.wharton: For who maketh thee to differ [from another]? and what hast thou that thou didst not receive? now if thou didst receive [it], why dost thou glory, as if thou hadst not received [it]?

textMismatch.clean: [We] [are] troubled on every side, yet not distressed; [we] [are] perplexed, but not in despair;
textMismatch.wharton: Now ye are full, now ye are rich, ye have reigned as kings without us: and I would to God ye did reign, that we also might reign with you.

textMismatch.clean: Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;
textMismatch.wharton: For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.

textMismatch.clean: Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body.
textMismatch.wharton: We [are] fools for Christs sake, but ye [are] wise in Christ; we [are] weak, but ye [are] strong; ye [are] honourable, but we [are] despised.

textMismatch.clean: For we which live are alway delivered unto death for Jesus sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh.
textMismatch.wharton: Even unto this present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwellingplace;

textMismatch.clean: So then death worketh in us, but life in you.
textMismatch.wharton: And labour, working with our own hands: being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it:

textMismatch.clean: We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak;
textMismatch.wharton: Being defamed, we intreat: we are made as the filth of the world, [and are] the offscouring of all things unto this day.

textMismatch.clean: Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present [us] with you.
textMismatch.wharton: I write not these things to shame you, but as my beloved sons I warn [you].

textMismatch.clean: For all things [are] for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.
textMismatch.wharton: For though ye have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet [have ye] not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel.

textMismatch.clean: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward [man] is renewed day by day.
