textMismatch.wharton: Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.

textMismatch.clean: And came and preached peace to you which were afar off, and to them that were nigh.
textMismatch.wharton: But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, [is] therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid.

textMismatch.clean: For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.
textMismatch.wharton: For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor.

textMismatch.clean: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
textMismatch.wharton: For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God.

textMismatch.clean: And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner [stone;]
textMismatch.wharton: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.

textMismatch.clean: In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord:
textMismatch.wharton: I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness [come] by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.

textMismatch.clean: FOR this cause I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles,
textMismatch.wharton: O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?

textMismatch.clean: If ye have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which is given me to you-ward:
textMismatch.wharton: This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

textMismatch.clean: How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote afore in few words,
textMismatch.wharton: Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh?

textMismatch.clean: Whereby, when ye read, ye may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ)
textMismatch.wharton: Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if [it be] yet in vain.

textMismatch.clean: Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit;
textMismatch.wharton: He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, [doeth he it] by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

textMismatch.clean: That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel:
textMismatch.wharton: Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.

textMismatch.clean: Whereof I was made a minister, according to the gift of the grace of God given unto me by the effectual working of his power.
textMismatch.wharton: Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.

textMismatch.clean: Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ;
textMismatch.wharton: And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, [saying], In thee shall all nations be blessed.

textMismatch.clean: And to make all [men] see what [is] the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ:
textMismatch.wharton: So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

textMismatch.clean: To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly [places] might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God,
textMismatch.wharton: For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed [is] every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.

textMismatch.clean: According to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord:
textMismatch.wharton: But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, [it is] evident: for, The just shall live by faith.

textMismatch.clean: In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.
textMismatch.wharton: And the law is not of faith: but, The man that doeth them shall live in them.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore I desire that ye faint not at my tribulations for you, which is your glory.
textMismatch.wharton: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed [is] every one that hangeth on a tree:

textMismatch.clean: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
textMismatch.wharton: That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

textMismatch.clean: Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named,
textMismatch.wharton: Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; Though [it be] but a mans covenant, yet [if it be] confirmed, no man disannulleth, or addeth thereto.

textMismatch.clean: That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;
textMismatch.wharton: Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.

textMismatch.clean: That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love,
textMismatch.wharton: And this I say, [that] the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.

textMismatch.clean: May be able to comprehend with all saints what [is] the breadth, and length, and depth, and height;
textMismatch.wharton: For if the inheritance [be] of the law, [it is] no more of promise: but God gave [it] to Abraham by promise.

textMismatch.clean: And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore then [serveth] the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; [and it was] ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.

textMismatch.clean: Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us,
textMismatch.wharton: Now a mediator is not [a mediator] of one, but God is one.

textMismatch.clean: Unto him [be] glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.
textMismatch.wharton: [Is] the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law.

textMismatch.clean: BE ye therefore followers of God, as dear children;
textMismatch.wharton: Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.

textMismatch.clean: And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.
textMismatch.wharton: Behold, I Paul say unto you, that if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.

textMismatch.clean: But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints;
textMismatch.wharton: For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.

textMismatch.clean: Neither filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting, which are not convenient: but rather giving of thanks.
textMismatch.wharton: Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.

textMismatch.clean: For this ye know, that no whoremonger, nor unclean person, nor covetous man, who is an idolater, hath any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.
textMismatch.wharton: For we through the Spirit wait for the hope of righteousness by faith.

textMismatch.clean: Let no man deceive you with vain words: for because of these things cometh the wrath of God upon the children of disobedience.
textMismatch.wharton: For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love.

textMismatch.clean: Be not ye therefore partakers with them.
textMismatch.wharton: Ye did run well; who did hinder you that ye should not obey the truth?

textMismatch.clean: For ye were sometimes darkness, but now [are] [ye] light in the Lord: walk as children of light:
textMismatch.wharton: This persuasion [cometh] not of him that calleth you.

textMismatch.clean: (For the fruit of the Spirit [is] in all goodness and righteousness and truth;)
textMismatch.wharton: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.

textMismatch.clean: Proving what is acceptable unto the Lord.
textMismatch.wharton: I have confidence in you through the Lord, that ye will be none otherwise minded: but he that troubleth you shall bear his judgment, whosoever he be.

textMismatch.clean: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove [them].
textMismatch.wharton: And I, brethren, if I yet preach circumcision, why do I yet suffer persecution? then is the offence of the cross ceased.

textMismatch.clean: For it is a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret.
textMismatch.wharton: I would they were even cut off which trouble you.

textMismatch.clean: But all things that are reproved are made manifest by the light: for whatsoever doth make manifest is light.
textMismatch.wharton: For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only [use] not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore he saith, Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light.
textMismatch.wharton: For all the law is fulfilled in one word, [even] in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

textMismatch.clean: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise,
textMismatch.wharton: But if ye bite and devour one another, take heed that ye be not consumed one of another.

textMismatch.clean: Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
textMismatch.wharton: [This] I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore be ye not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord [is].
textMismatch.wharton: For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would.

textMismatch.clean: And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit;
textMismatch.wharton: But if ye be led of the Spirit, ye are not under the law.

textMismatch.clean: Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord;
textMismatch.wharton: Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are [these]; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,

textMismatch.clean: Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ;
textMismatch.wharton: Idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies,

textMismatch.clean: Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God.
textMismatch.wharton: Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told [you] in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

textMismatch.clean: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.
textMismatch.wharton: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

textMismatch.clean: For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.
textMismatch.wharton: Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.

textMismatch.clean: Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so [let] the wives [be] to their own husbands in every thing.
textMismatch.wharton: And they that are Christs have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.

textMismatch.clean: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;
textMismatch.wharton: If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.

textMismatch.clean: That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word,
textMismatch.wharton: Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.

textMismatch.clean: CHILDREN, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.
textMismatch.wharton: Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.

textMismatch.clean: Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)
textMismatch.wharton: Bear ye one anothers burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

textMismatch.clean: That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.
textMismatch.wharton: For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.

textMismatch.clean: And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
textMismatch.wharton: But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another.

textMismatch.clean: Servants, be obedient to them that are [your] masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ;
textMismatch.wharton: For every man shall bear his own burden.

textMismatch.clean: Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart;
textMismatch.wharton: Let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things.

textMismatch.clean: With good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men:
textMismatch.wharton: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.

textMismatch.clean: Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether [he] [be] bond or free.
textMismatch.wharton: For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.

textMismatch.clean: And, ye masters, do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him.
textMismatch.wharton: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.

textMismatch.clean: Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might.
textMismatch.wharton: As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all [men], especially unto them who are of the household of faith.

textMismatch.clean: Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
textMismatch.wharton: Ye see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand.

textMismatch.clean: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high [places].
textMismatch.wharton: As many as desire to make a fair shew in the flesh, they constrain you to be circumcised; only lest they should suffer persecution for the cross of Christ.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.
textMismatch.wharton: For neither they themselves who are circumcised keep the law; but desire to have you circumcised, that they may glory in your flesh.

textMismatch.clean: Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness;
textMismatch.wharton: But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world.

textMismatch.clean: And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace;
textMismatch.wharton: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature.

textMismatch.clean: Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.
textMismatch.wharton: And as many as walk according to this rule, peace [be] on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.

textMismatch.clean: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God:
textMismatch.wharton: From henceforth let no man trouble me: for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus.

textMismatch.clean: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints;
textMismatch.wharton: Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with your spirit. Amen.

textMismatch.clean: PAUL and Timotheus, the servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus which are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons:
textMismatch.wharton: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus:

textMismatch.clean: Grace [be] unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and [from] the Lord Jesus Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Grace [be] to you, and peace, from God our Father, and [from] the Lord Jesus Christ.

textMismatch.clean: I thank my God upon every remembrance of you,
textMismatch.wharton: Blessed [be] the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly [places] in Christ:

textMismatch.clean: Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy,
textMismatch.wharton: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:

textMismatch.clean: For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now;
textMismatch.wharton: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,

textMismatch.clean: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform [it] until the day of Jesus Christ:
textMismatch.wharton: To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved.

textMismatch.clean: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace.
textMismatch.wharton: In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace;

textMismatch.clean: For God is my record, how greatly I long after you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherein he hath abounded toward us in all wisdom and prudence;

textMismatch.clean: And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and [in] all judgment;
textMismatch.wharton: Having made known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he hath purposed in himself:

textMismatch.clean: That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ;
textMismatch.wharton: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; [even] in him:

textMismatch.clean: Being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are by Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.
textMismatch.wharton: In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will:

textMismatch.clean: But I would ye should understand, brethren, that the things [which] [happened] unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel;
textMismatch.wharton: That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ.

textMismatch.clean: So that my bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace, and in all other [places;]
textMismatch.wharton: In whom ye also [trusted], after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise,

textMismatch.clean: And many of the brethren in the Lord, waxing confident by my bonds, are much more bold to speak the word without fear.
textMismatch.wharton: Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.

textMismatch.clean: Some indeed preach Christ even of envy and strife; and some also of good will:
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore I also, after I heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus, and love unto all the saints,

textMismatch.clean: The one preach Christ of contention, not sincerely, supposing to add affliction to my bonds:
textMismatch.wharton: Cease not to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers;

textMismatch.clean: But the other of love, knowing that I am set for the defence of the gospel.
textMismatch.wharton: That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him:

textMismatch.clean: What then? notwithstanding, every way, whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice, yea, and will rejoice.
textMismatch.wharton: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints,

textMismatch.clean: For I know that this shall turn to my salvation through your prayer, and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
textMismatch.wharton: And what [is] the exceeding greatness of his power to us-ward who believe, according to the working of his mighty power,

textMismatch.clean: According to my earnest expectation and [my] hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed, but [that] with all boldness, as always, [so] now also Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether [it] [be] by life, or by death.
textMismatch.wharton: Which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set [him] at his own right hand in the heavenly [places],

textMismatch.clean: For to me to live [is] Christ, and to die [is] gain.
textMismatch.wharton: Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come:

textMismatch.clean: But if I live in the flesh, this [is] the fruit of my labour: yet what I shall choose I wot not.
textMismatch.wharton: And hath put all [things] under his feet, and gave him [to be] the head over all [things] to the church,

textMismatch.clean: For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better:
textMismatch.wharton: Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.

textMismatch.clean: IF [there] [be] therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any bowels and mercies,
textMismatch.wharton: And you [hath he quickened], who were dead in trespasses and sins;

textMismatch.clean: Fulfil ye my joy, that ye be likeminded, having the same love, [being] of one accord, of one mind.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience:

textMismatch.clean: [Let] nothing [be] [done] through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
textMismatch.wharton: Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others.

textMismatch.clean: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.
textMismatch.wharton: But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us,

textMismatch.clean: Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus:
textMismatch.wharton: Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;)

textMismatch.clean: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God:
textMismatch.wharton: And hath raised [us] up together, and made [us] sit together in heavenly [places] in Christ Jesus:

textMismatch.clean: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:
textMismatch.wharton: That in the ages to come he might shew the exceeding riches of his grace in [his] kindness toward us through Christ Jesus.

textMismatch.clean: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.
textMismatch.wharton: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: [it is] the gift of God:

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name:
textMismatch.wharton: Not of works, lest any man should boast.

textMismatch.clean: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of [things] in heaven, and [things] in earth, and [things] under the earth;
textMismatch.wharton: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.

textMismatch.clean: And [that] every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ [is] Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore remember, that ye [being] in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands;

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
textMismatch.wharton: That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world:

textMismatch.clean: For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of [his] good pleasure.
textMismatch.wharton: But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.

textMismatch.clean: Do all things without murmurings and disputings:
textMismatch.wharton: For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition [between us];

textMismatch.clean: That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world;
textMismatch.wharton: Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, [even] the law of commandments [contained] in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, [so] making peace;

textMismatch.clean: Holding forth the word of life; that I may rejoice in the day of Christ, that I have not run in vain, neither laboured in vain.
textMismatch.wharton: And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby:

textMismatch.clean: Yea, and if I be offered upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I joy, and rejoice with you all.
textMismatch.wharton: And came and preached peace to you which were afar off, and to them that were nigh.

textMismatch.clean: For the same cause also do ye joy, and rejoice with me.
textMismatch.wharton: For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.

textMismatch.clean: But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timotheus shortly unto you, that I also may be of good comfort, when I know your state.
textMismatch.wharton: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;

textMismatch.clean: For I have no man likeminded, who will naturally care for your state.
textMismatch.wharton: And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner [stone];

textMismatch.clean: For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christs.
textMismatch.wharton: In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord:

textMismatch.clean: But ye know the proof of him, that, as a son with the father, he hath served with me in the gospel.
textMismatch.wharton: In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.

textMismatch.clean: FINALLY, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed [is] not grievous, but for you [it] [is] safe.
textMismatch.wharton: For this cause I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles,

textMismatch.clean: Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision.
textMismatch.wharton: If ye have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which is given me to you-ward:

textMismatch.clean: For we are the circumcision, which worship God in the spirit, and rejoice in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh.
textMismatch.wharton: How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote afore in few words,

textMismatch.clean: Though I might also have confidence in the flesh. If any other man thinketh that he hath whereof he might trust in the flesh, I more:
textMismatch.wharton: Whereby, when ye read, ye may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ)

textMismatch.clean: Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, [of] the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee;
textMismatch.wharton: Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit;

textMismatch.clean: Concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless.
textMismatch.wharton: That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel:

textMismatch.clean: But what things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Whereof I was made a minister, according to the gift of the grace of God given unto me by the effectual working of his power.

textMismatch.clean: Yea doubtless, and I count all things [but] loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them [but] dung, that I may win Christ,
textMismatch.wharton: Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ;

textMismatch.clean: And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith:
textMismatch.wharton: And to make all [men] see what [is] the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ:

textMismatch.clean: That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death;
textMismatch.wharton: To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly [places] might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God,

textMismatch.clean: If by any means I might attain unto the resurrection of the dead.
textMismatch.wharton: According to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord:

textMismatch.clean: Not as though I had already attained, either were already perfect: but I follow after, if that I may apprehend that for which also I am apprehended of Christ Jesus.
textMismatch.wharton: In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.

textMismatch.clean: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but [this] one thing [I] [do], forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore I desire that ye faint not at my tribulations for you, which is your glory.

textMismatch.clean: I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
textMismatch.wharton: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,

textMismatch.clean: Let us therefore, as many as be perfect, be thus minded: and if in any thing ye be otherwise minded, God shall reveal even this unto you.
textMismatch.wharton: Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named,

textMismatch.clean: Nevertheless, whereto we have already attained, let us walk by the same rule, let us mind the same thing.
textMismatch.wharton: That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;

textMismatch.clean: Brethren, be followers together of me, and mark them which walk so as ye have us for an ensample.
textMismatch.wharton: That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love,

textMismatch.clean: (For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, [that] [they] [are] the enemies of the cross of Christ:
textMismatch.wharton: May be able to comprehend with all saints what [is] the breadth, and length, and depth, and height;

textMismatch.clean: Whose end [is] destruction, whose God [is] [their] belly, and [whose] glory [is] in their shame, who mind earthly things.)
textMismatch.wharton: And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.

textMismatch.clean: For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ:
textMismatch.wharton: Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us,

textMismatch.clean: Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body, according to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself.
textMismatch.wharton: Unto him [be] glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.

textMismatch.clean: THEREFORE, my brethren dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord, [my] dearly beloved.
textMismatch.wharton: I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called,

textMismatch.clean: I beseech Euodias, and beseech Syntyche, that they be of the same mind in the Lord.
textMismatch.wharton: With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love;

textMismatch.clean: And I intreat thee also, true yokefellow, help those women which laboured with me in the gospel, with Clement also, and [with] other my fellowlabourers, whose names [are] in the book of life.
textMismatch.wharton: Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

textMismatch.clean: Rejoice in the Lord alway: [and] again I say, Rejoice.
textMismatch.wharton: [There is] one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling;

textMismatch.clean: Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord [is] at hand.
textMismatch.wharton: One Lord, one faith, one baptism,

textMismatch.clean: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
textMismatch.wharton: One God and Father of all, who [is] above all, and through all, and in you all.

textMismatch.clean: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
textMismatch.wharton: But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.

textMismatch.clean: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things [are] honest, whatsoever things [are] just, whatsoever things [are] pure, whatsoever things [are] lovely, whatsoever things [are] of good report; if [there] [be] any virtue, and if [there] [be] any praise, think on these things.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men.

textMismatch.clean: Those things, which ye have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, do: and the God of peace shall be with you.
textMismatch.wharton: (Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?

textMismatch.clean: But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at the last your care of me hath flourished again; wherein ye were also careful, but ye lacked opportunity.
textMismatch.wharton: He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.)

textMismatch.clean: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, [therewith] to be content.
textMismatch.wharton: And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers;

textMismatch.clean: I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.
textMismatch.wharton: For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ:

textMismatch.clean: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
textMismatch.wharton: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ:

textMismatch.clean: Notwithstanding ye have well done, that ye did communicate with my affliction.
textMismatch.wharton: That we [henceforth] be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, [and] cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive;

textMismatch.clean: Now ye Philippians know also, that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with me as concerning giving and receiving, but ye only.
textMismatch.wharton: But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, [even] Christ:

textMismatch.clean: For even in Thessalonica ye sent once and again unto my necessity.
textMismatch.wharton: From whom the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth, according to the effectual working in the measure of every part, maketh increase of the body unto the edifying of itself in love.

textMismatch.clean: Not because I desire a gift: but I desire fruit that may abound to your account.
textMismatch.wharton: This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that ye henceforth walk not as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind,

textMismatch.clean: But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things [which] [were] [sent] from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.
textMismatch.wharton: Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their heart:

textMismatch.clean: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
textMismatch.wharton: Who being past feeling have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness.

textMismatch.clean: Now unto God and our Father [be] glory for ever and ever. Amen.
textMismatch.wharton: But ye have not so learned Christ;

textMismatch.clean: Salute every saint in Christ Jesus. The brethren which are with me greet you.
textMismatch.wharton: If so be that ye have heard him, and have been taught by him, as the truth is in Jesus:

textMismatch.clean: All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Cæsars household.
textMismatch.wharton: That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts;

textMismatch.clean: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen.
textMismatch.wharton: And be renewed in the spirit of your mind;

textMismatch.clean: PAUL, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timotheus [our] brother,
textMismatch.wharton: Paul and Timotheus, the servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus which are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons:

textMismatch.clean: To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse: Grace [be] unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Grace [be] unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and [from] the Lord Jesus Christ.

textMismatch.clean: We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you,
textMismatch.wharton: I thank my God upon every remembrance of you,

textMismatch.clean: Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love [which] [ye] [have] to all the saints,
textMismatch.wharton: Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy,

textMismatch.clean: For the hope which is laid up for you in heaven, whereof ye heard before in the word of the truth of the gospel;
textMismatch.wharton: For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now;

textMismatch.clean: Which is come unto you, as [it] [is] in all the world; and bringeth forth fruit, as [it] [doth] also in you, since the day ye heard [of] [it], and knew the grace of God in truth:
textMismatch.wharton: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform [it] until the day of Jesus Christ:

textMismatch.clean: As ye also learned of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ;
textMismatch.wharton: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace.

textMismatch.clean: Who also declared unto us your love in the Spirit.
textMismatch.wharton: For God is my record, how greatly I long after you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ.

textMismatch.clean: For this cause we also, since the day we heard [it], do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;
textMismatch.wharton: And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and [in] all judgment;

textMismatch.clean: That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;
textMismatch.wharton: That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ;

textMismatch.clean: Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness;
textMismatch.wharton: Being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are by Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.

textMismatch.clean: Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light:
textMismatch.wharton: But I would ye should understand, brethren, that the things [which happened] unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel;

textMismatch.clean: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated [us] into the kingdom of his dear Son:
textMismatch.wharton: So that my bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace, and in all other [places];

textMismatch.clean: In whom we have redemption through his blood, [even] the forgiveness of sins:
textMismatch.wharton: And many of the brethren in the Lord, waxing confident by my bonds, are much more bold to speak the word without fear.

textMismatch.clean: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature:
textMismatch.wharton: Some indeed preach Christ even of envy and strife; and some also of good will:

textMismatch.clean: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether [they] [be] thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:
textMismatch.wharton: The one preach Christ of contention, not sincerely, supposing to add affliction to my bonds:

textMismatch.clean: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.
textMismatch.wharton: But the other of love, knowing that I am set for the defence of the gospel.

textMismatch.clean: And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all [things] he might have the preeminence.
textMismatch.wharton: What then? notwithstanding, every way, whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice, yea, and will rejoice.

textMismatch.clean: For it pleased [the] [Father] that in him should all fulness dwell;
textMismatch.wharton: For I know that this shall turn to my salvation through your prayer, and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,

textMismatch.clean: And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, [I] [say], whether [they] [be] things in earth, or things in heaven.
textMismatch.wharton: According to my earnest expectation and [my] hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed, but [that] with all boldness, as always, [so] now also Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether [it be] by life, or by death.

textMismatch.clean: And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in [your] mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled
textMismatch.wharton: For to me to live [is] Christ, and to die [is] gain.

textMismatch.clean: In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight:
textMismatch.wharton: But if I live in the flesh, this [is] the fruit of my labour: yet what I shall choose I wot not.

textMismatch.clean: If ye continue in the faith grounded and settled, and [be] not moved away from the hope of the gospel, which ye have heard, [and] which was preached to every creature which is under heaven; whereof I Paul am made a minister;
textMismatch.wharton: For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better:

textMismatch.clean: Who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his bodys sake, which is the church:
textMismatch.wharton: Nevertheless to abide in the flesh [is] more needful for you.

textMismatch.clean: Whereof I am made a minister, according to the dispensation of God which is given to me for you, to fulfil the word of God;
textMismatch.wharton: And having this confidence, I know that I shall abide and continue with you all for your furtherance and joy of faith;

textMismatch.clean: [Even] the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints:
textMismatch.wharton: That your rejoicing may be more abundant in Jesus Christ for me by my coming to you again.

textMismatch.clean: To whom God would make known what [is] the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory:
textMismatch.wharton: Only let your conversation be as it becometh the gospel of Christ: that whether I come and see you, or else be absent, I may hear of your affairs, that ye stand fast in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel;

textMismatch.clean: Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom; that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus:
textMismatch.wharton: And in nothing terrified by your adversaries: which is to them an evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that of God.

textMismatch.clean: Whereunto I also labour, striving according to his working, which worketh in me mightily.
textMismatch.wharton: For unto you it is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on him, but also to suffer for his sake;

textMismatch.clean: FOR I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and [for] them at Laodicea, and [for] as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;
textMismatch.wharton: If [there be] therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any bowels and mercies,

textMismatch.clean: That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ;

textMismatch.clean: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
textMismatch.wharton: [Let] nothing [be done] through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.

textMismatch.clean: And this I say, lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.
textMismatch.wharton: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.

textMismatch.clean: For though I be absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, joying and beholding your order, and the stedfastness of your faith in Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus:

textMismatch.clean: As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, [so] walk ye in him:
textMismatch.wharton: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God:

textMismatch.clean: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.
textMismatch.wharton: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:

textMismatch.clean: Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.

textMismatch.clean: For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.

textMismatch.wharton: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of [things] in heaven, and [things] in earth, and [things] under the earth;

textMismatch.wharton: And [that] every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ [is] Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

textMismatch.clean: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with [him] through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

textMismatch.clean: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross;
textMismatch.wharton: Do all things without murmurings and disputings:

textMismatch.wharton: That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world;

textMismatch.clean: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body [is] of Christ.

textMismatch.wharton: That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death;

textMismatch.wharton: Therefore, my brethren dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord, [my] dearly beloved.

textMismatch.clean: That I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak.

textMismatch.clean: PAUL, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians [which] [is] in God the Father and [in] the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace [be] unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timotheus [our] brother,

textMismatch.wharton: To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse: Grace [be] unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

textMismatch.clean: Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love, and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, in the sight of God and our Father;
textMismatch.wharton: We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you,

textMismatch.wharton: As ye also learned of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ;

textMismatch.wharton: Who also declared unto us your love in the Spirit.

textMismatch.clean: For they themselves shew of us what manner of entering in we had unto you, and how ye turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God;
textMismatch.wharton: For this cause we also, since the day we heard [it], do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;

textMismatch.clean: And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, [even] Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.
textMismatch.wharton: That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;

textMismatch.clean: FOR yourselves, brethren, know our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain:
textMismatch.wharton: For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and [for] them at Laodicea, and [for] as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;

textMismatch.clean: But even after that we had suffered before, and were shamefully entreated, as ye know, at Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak unto you the gospel of God with much contention.
textMismatch.wharton: That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ;

textMismatch.clean: For our exhortation [was] not of deceit, nor of uncleanness, nor in guile:
textMismatch.wharton: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.

textMismatch.clean: But as we were allowed of God to be put in trust with the gospel, even so we speak; not as pleasing men, but God, which trieth our hearts.
textMismatch.wharton: And this I say, lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.

textMismatch.clean: For neither at any time used we flattering words, as ye know, nor a cloke of covetousness; God [is] witness:
textMismatch.wharton: For though I be absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, joying and beholding your order, and the stedfastness of your faith in Christ.

textMismatch.wharton: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.

textMismatch.wharton: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with [him] through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.

textMismatch.wharton: And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, hath he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses;
