textMismatch.clean: Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.
textMismatch.wharton: But ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?

textMismatch.clean: Unto you therefore which believe [he] [is] precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner,
textMismatch.wharton: Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?

textMismatch.clean: And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, [even] [to] [them] which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.
textMismatch.wharton: If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well:

textMismatch.clean: But ye [are] a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
textMismatch.wharton: But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.

textMismatch.clean: Which in time past [were] not a people, but [are] now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.
textMismatch.wharton: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one [point], he is guilty of all.

textMismatch.clean: Dearly beloved, I beseech [you] as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul;
textMismatch.wharton: For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law.

textMismatch.clean: Having your conversation honest among the Gentiles: that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may by [your] good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation.
textMismatch.wharton: So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.

textMismatch.clean: Submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lords sake: whether it be to the king, as supreme;
textMismatch.wharton: For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.

textMismatch.clean: Or unto governors, as unto them that are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers, and for the praise of them that do well.
textMismatch.wharton: What [doth it] profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?

textMismatch.clean: For so is the will of God, that with well doing ye may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men:
textMismatch.wharton: If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,

textMismatch.clean: As free, and not using [your] liberty for a cloke of maliciousness, but as the servants of God.
textMismatch.wharton: And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be [ye] warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what [doth it] profit?

textMismatch.clean: Honour all [men]. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king.
textMismatch.wharton: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.

textMismatch.clean: Servants, [be] subject to [your] masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.
textMismatch.wharton: Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.

textMismatch.clean: For this [is] thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.
textMismatch.wharton: Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.

textMismatch.clean: For what glory [is] [it], if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer [for] [it], ye take it patiently, this [is] acceptable with God.
textMismatch.wharton: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?

textMismatch.clean: For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps:
textMismatch.wharton: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?

textMismatch.clean: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth:
textMismatch.wharton: Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?

textMismatch.clean: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed [himself] to him that judgeth righteously:
textMismatch.wharton: And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.

textMismatch.clean: Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.
textMismatch.wharton: Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.

textMismatch.clean: For ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.
textMismatch.wharton: Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent [them] out another way?

textMismatch.clean: LIKEWISE, ye wives, [be] in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives;
textMismatch.wharton: My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.

textMismatch.clean: While they behold your chaste conversation [coupled] with fear.
textMismatch.wharton: For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same [is] a perfect man, [and] able also to bridle the whole body.

textMismatch.clean: Whose adorning let it not be that outward [adorning] of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel;
textMismatch.wharton: Behold, we put bits in the horses mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.

textMismatch.clean: But [let] [it] [be] the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, [even] [the] [ornament] of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.
textMismatch.wharton: Behold also the ships, which though [they be] so great, and [are] driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth.

textMismatch.clean: For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands:
textMismatch.wharton: Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!

textMismatch.clean: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement.
textMismatch.wharton: And the tongue [is] a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.

textMismatch.clean: Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with [them] according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.
textMismatch.wharton: For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed of mankind:

textMismatch.clean: Finally, [be] [ye] all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, [be] pitiful, [be] courteous:
textMismatch.wharton: But the tongue can no man tame; [it is] an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.

textMismatch.clean: Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.
textMismatch.wharton: Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God.

textMismatch.clean: For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile:
textMismatch.wharton: Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.

textMismatch.clean: Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.
textMismatch.wharton: Doth a fountain send forth at the same place sweet [water] and bitter?

textMismatch.clean: For the eyes of the Lord [are] over the righteous, and his ears [are] [open] unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord [is] against them that do evil.
textMismatch.wharton: Can the fig tree, my brethren, bear olive berries? either a vine, figs? so [can] no fountain both yield salt water and fresh.

textMismatch.clean: And who [is] he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?
textMismatch.wharton: Who [is] a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.

textMismatch.clean: But and if ye suffer for righteousness sake, happy [are] [ye:] and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;
textMismatch.wharton: But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth.

textMismatch.clean: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and [be] ready always to [give] an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
textMismatch.wharton: This wisdom descendeth not from above, but [is] earthly, sensual, devilish.

textMismatch.clean: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: For where envying and strife [is], there [is] confusion and every evil work.

textMismatch.clean: For [it] [is] better, if the will of God be so, that ye suffer for well doing, than for evil doing.
textMismatch.wharton: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, [and] easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.

textMismatch.clean: For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:
textMismatch.wharton: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace.

textMismatch.clean: FORASMUCH then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind: for he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin;
textMismatch.wharton: From whence [come] wars and fightings among you? [come they] not hence, [even] of your lusts that war in your members?

textMismatch.clean: That he no longer should live the rest of [his] time in the flesh to the lusts of men, but to the will of God.
textMismatch.wharton: Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.

textMismatch.clean: For the time past of [our] life may suffice us to have wrought the will of the Gentiles, when we walked in lasciviousness, lusts, excess of wine, revellings, banquetings, and abominable idolatries:
textMismatch.wharton: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume [it] upon your lusts.

textMismatch.clean: Wherein they think it strange that ye run not with [them] to the same excess of riot, speaking evil of [you:]
textMismatch.wharton: Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.

textMismatch.clean: Who shall give account to him that is ready to judge the quick and the dead.
textMismatch.wharton: Do ye think that the scripture saith in vain, The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy?

textMismatch.clean: For for this cause was the gospel preached also to them that are dead, that they might be judged according to men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit.
textMismatch.wharton: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.

textMismatch.clean: But the end of all things is at hand: be ye therefore sober, and watch unto prayer.
textMismatch.wharton: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

textMismatch.clean: And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.
textMismatch.wharton: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse [your] hands, [ye] sinners; and purify [your] hearts, [ye] double minded.

textMismatch.clean: Use hospitality one to another without grudging.
textMismatch.wharton: Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and [your] joy to heaviness.

textMismatch.clean: As every man hath received the gift, [even] [so] minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.
textMismatch.wharton: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.

textMismatch.clean: If any man speak, [let] [him] [speak] as the oracles of God; if any man minister, [let] [him] [do] [it] as of the ability which God giveth: that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be praise and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.
textMismatch.wharton: Speak not evil one of another, brethren. He that speaketh evil of [his] brother, and judgeth his brother, speaketh evil of the law, and judgeth the law: but if thou judge the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge.

textMismatch.clean: Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you:
textMismatch.wharton: There is one lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy: who art thou that judgest another?

textMismatch.clean: But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christs sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.
textMismatch.wharton: Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain:

textMismatch.clean: If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy [are] [ye;] for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.
textMismatch.wharton: Whereas ye know not what [shall be] on the morrow. For what [is] your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.

textMismatch.clean: But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or [as] a thief, or [as] an evildoer, or as a busybody in other mens matters.
textMismatch.wharton: For that ye [ought] to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.

textMismatch.clean: Yet if [any] [man] [suffer] as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.
textMismatch.wharton: But now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.

textMismatch.clean: For the time [is] [come] that judgment must begin at the house of God: and if [it] first [begin] at us, what shall the end [be] of them that obey not the gospel of God?
textMismatch.wharton: Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth [it] not, to him it is sin.

textMismatch.clean: THE elders which are among you I exhort, who am also an elder, and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a partaker of the glory that shall be revealed:
textMismatch.wharton: Go to now, [ye] rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon [you].

textMismatch.clean: Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight [thereof], not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind;
textMismatch.wharton: Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are motheaten.

textMismatch.clean: Neither as being lords over [God][s] heritage, but being ensamples to the flock.
textMismatch.wharton: Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.

textMismatch.clean: And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.
textMismatch.wharton: Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth.

textMismatch.clean: Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all [of] [you] be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.
textMismatch.wharton: Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter.

textMismatch.clean: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time:
textMismatch.wharton: Ye have condemned [and] killed the just; [and] he doth not resist you.

textMismatch.clean: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
textMismatch.wharton: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.

textMismatch.clean: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:
textMismatch.wharton: Be ye also patient; stablish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord draweth nigh.

textMismatch.clean: Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.
textMismatch.wharton: Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest ye be condemned: behold, the judge standeth before the door.

textMismatch.clean: But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle [you].
textMismatch.wharton: Take, my brethren, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction, and of patience.

textMismatch.clean: To him [be] glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.
textMismatch.wharton: Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.

textMismatch.clean: By Silvanus, a faithful brother unto you, as I suppose, I have written briefly, exhorting, and testifying that this is the true grace of God wherein ye stand.
textMismatch.wharton: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and [your] nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.

textMismatch.clean: The [church] [that] [is] at Babylon, elected together with [you], saluteth you; and [so] [doth] Marcus my son.
textMismatch.wharton: Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.

textMismatch.clean: Greet ye one another with a kiss of charity. Peace [be] with you all that are in Christ Jesus. Amen.
textMismatch.wharton: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord:

textMismatch.clean: SIMON Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to them that have obtained like precious faith with us through the righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ:
textMismatch.wharton: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,

textMismatch.clean: Grace and peace be multiplied unto you through the knowledge of God, and of Jesus our Lord,
textMismatch.wharton: Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace unto you, and peace, be multiplied.

textMismatch.clean: According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that [pertain] unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue:
textMismatch.wharton: Blessed [be] the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

textMismatch.clean: Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
textMismatch.wharton: To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you,

textMismatch.clean: And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge;
textMismatch.wharton: Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

textMismatch.clean: And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness;
textMismatch.wharton: Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations:

textMismatch.clean: And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.
textMismatch.wharton: That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ:

textMismatch.clean: For if these things be in you, and abound, they make [you] [that] [ye] [shall] neither [be] barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see [him] not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory:

textMismatch.clean: But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.
textMismatch.wharton: Receiving the end of your faith, [even] the salvation of [your] souls.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall:
textMismatch.wharton: Of which salvation the prophets have inquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace [that should come] unto you:

textMismatch.clean: For so an entrance shall be ministered unto you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore I will not be negligent to put you always in remembrance of these things, though ye know [them], and be established in the present truth.
textMismatch.wharton: Unto whom it was revealed, that not unto themselves, but unto us they did minister the things, which are now reported unto you by them that have preached the gospel unto you with the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven; which things the angels desire to look into.

textMismatch.clean: Yea, I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting [you] in remembrance;
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;

textMismatch.clean: Knowing that shortly I must put off [this] my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me.
textMismatch.wharton: As obedient children, not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts in your ignorance:

textMismatch.clean: Moreover I will endeavour that ye may be able after my decease to have these things always in remembrance.
textMismatch.wharton: But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;

textMismatch.clean: For we have not followed cunningly devised fables, when we made known unto you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but were eyewitnesses of his majesty.
textMismatch.wharton: Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy.

textMismatch.clean: For he received from God the Father honour and glory, when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
textMismatch.wharton: And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every mans work, pass the time of your sojourning [here] in fear:

textMismatch.clean: And this voice which came from heaven we heard, when we were with him in the holy mount.
textMismatch.wharton: Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, [as] silver and gold, from your vain conversation [received] by tradition from your fathers;

textMismatch.clean: We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:
textMismatch.wharton: But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot:

textMismatch.clean: Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.
textMismatch.wharton: Who verily was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you,

textMismatch.clean: For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake [as] [they] [were] moved by the Holy Ghost.
textMismatch.wharton: Who by him do believe in God, that raised him up from the dead, and gave him glory; that your faith and hope might be in God.

textMismatch.clean: BUT there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings,

textMismatch.clean: And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of.
textMismatch.wharton: As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:

textMismatch.clean: And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not.
textMismatch.wharton: If so be ye have tasted that the Lord [is] gracious.

textMismatch.clean: For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast [them] down to hell, and delivered [them] into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;
textMismatch.wharton: To whom coming, [as unto] a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, [and] precious,

textMismatch.clean: And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth [person], a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;
textMismatch.wharton: Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.

textMismatch.clean: And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned [them] with an overthrow, making [them] an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.

textMismatch.clean: And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked:
textMismatch.wharton: Unto you therefore which believe [he is] precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner,

textMismatch.clean: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed [his] righteous soul from day to day with [their] unlawful deeds;)
textMismatch.wharton: And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, [even to them] which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.

textMismatch.clean: The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished:
textMismatch.wharton: But ye [are] a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:

textMismatch.wharton: And now I beseech thee, lady, not as though I wrote a new commandment unto thee, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.

textMismatch.clean: Which have borne witness of thy charity before the church: whom if thou bring forward on their journey after a godly sort, thou shalt do well:
textMismatch.wharton: And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.

textMismatch.clean: Because that for his names sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles.
textMismatch.wharton: For many deceivers are entered into the world, who confess not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh. This is a deceiver and an antichrist.

textMismatch.clean: We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth.
textMismatch.wharton: Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward.

textMismatch.clean: I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.
textMismatch.wharton: Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of Christ, hath not God. He that abideth in the doctrine of Christ, he hath both the Father and the Son.

textMismatch.clean: Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth, prating against us with malicious words: and not content therewith, neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth [them] out of the church.
textMismatch.wharton: If there come any unto you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into [your] house, neither bid him God speed:

textMismatch.clean: Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.
textMismatch.wharton: For he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds.

textMismatch.clean: Demetrius hath good report of all [men], and of the truth itself: yea, and we [also] bear record; and ye know that our record is true.
textMismatch.wharton: Having many things to write unto you, I would not [write] with paper and ink: but I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full.

textMismatch.clean: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee:
textMismatch.wharton: The children of thy elect sister greet thee. Amen.

textMismatch.clean: JUDE, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, [and] called:
textMismatch.wharton: The elder unto the wellbeloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth.

textMismatch.clean: Mercy unto you, and peace, and love, be multiplied.
textMismatch.wharton: Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.

textMismatch.clean: Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort [you] that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.
textMismatch.wharton: For I rejoiced greatly, when the brethren came and testified of the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth.

textMismatch.clean: For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.
textMismatch.wharton: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.

textMismatch.clean: I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not.
textMismatch.wharton: Beloved, thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers;

textMismatch.clean: And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.
textMismatch.wharton: Which have borne witness of thy charity before the church: whom if thou bring forward on their journey after a godly sort, thou shalt do well:

textMismatch.clean: Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.
textMismatch.wharton: Because that for his names sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles.

textMismatch.clean: Likewise also these [filthy] dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.
textMismatch.wharton: We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth.

textMismatch.clean: Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee.
textMismatch.wharton: I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.

textMismatch.clean: But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves.
textMismatch.wharton: Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth, prating against us with malicious words: and not content therewith, neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth [them] out of the church.

textMismatch.clean: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.
textMismatch.wharton: Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.

textMismatch.clean: These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds [they] [are] without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots;
textMismatch.wharton: Demetrius hath good report of all [men], and of the truth itself: yea, and we [also] bear record; and ye know that our record is true.

textMismatch.clean: Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.
textMismatch.wharton: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee:

textMismatch.clean: And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints,
textMismatch.wharton: But I trust I shall shortly see thee, and we shall speak face to face. Peace [be] to thee. [Our] friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name.
